1"""
2dist_m4ri.py: Python wrapper for the multithreaded dist_m4ri distance calculator.
3
4Provides high-level APIs for computing:
5- Classical code distance: compute_classical_distance(...)
6- Single-sided quantum code distance: compute_quantum_distance(...)
7- CSS quantum code distance: compute_css_distance(...)
8- Detector Error Model (DEM) distance: compute_dem_distance(...)
9- Certified lower bound on the distance of a Stim memory circuit from its code-sized model:
10 compute_model_lower_bound(...)
11
12Supports distance caching, codeword export, and fallback/option for the codedistance library.
13Since dist_m4ri natively handles multithreading (via POSIX threads and dynamic bracketing),
14no Python-level threading or subprocess-per-core logic is necessary.
15"""

37# Debug bitmap (debug=N): bits 1..32768 are passed to the dist_m4ri binary (1: summary, 2: progress, 4: periodic
38# status, 8: thread allocation and timing, 16: code parameters, 32: codeword supports, 64: arguments, 128: matrices,
39# 256: codeword dump, 2048: no size cutoff; see its --morehelp), the higher bits are used by the Python wrapper only.
40PY_DBG_COMMANDS = 1 << 16 # echo the dist_m4ri command lines and their run times
41PY_DBG_CACHE = 1 << 17 # cache messages
42PY_DBG_CIRCUITS = 1 << 18 # Stim circuit to DEM conversion details
43PY_DBG_KEEP_FILES = 1 << 19 # keep (and list) the temporary matrix, codeword, and DEM files
44BIN_DBG_MASK = 0xFFFF # the debug bits passed to the dist_m4ri binary
45VERBOSE_DEBUG = 3 | PY_DBG_COMMANDS | PY_DBG_CACHE # debug bits implied by verbose=True (--verbose)

48def parse_debug_value(val: Union[str, int]) -> int:
49 """
50 Parses a debug bitmap value: a non-negative decimal or hexadecimal (0x...) integer, as in the dist_m4ri binary
51 (no octal: leading zeros are ignored).
52
53 Args:
54 val: The value, e.g., "3" or "0x10004", or an int.
55
56 Returns:
57 The debug bitmap.
58
59 Raises:
60 ValueError: If the value is not a non-negative integer.
61 """
62 msg = f"invalid debug={val!r}: expected a non-negative decimal or hexadecimal (0x...) integer"
63 if isinstance(val, bool):
64 raise ValueError(msg)
65 if isinstance(val, int):
66 value = val
67 else:
68 s = str(val).strip()
69 try:
70 value = int(s[2:], 16) if s.lower().startswith("0x") else int(s, 10)
71 except ValueError:
72 raise ValueError(msg) from None
73 if value < 0:
74 raise ValueError(msg)
75 return value

131def set_distance_cache_file(filepath: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None) -> None:
132 """
133 Sets the default JSON file for persistent distance caching.
134 If the file exists, its contents are loaded into memory.
135 """
136 global _distance_cache_file
137 if filepath is not None:
138 _distance_cache_file = str(Path(filepath).resolve())
139 load_distance_cache(_distance_cache_file)
140 else:
141 _distance_cache_file = None
142
143
144def load_distance_cache(filepath: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
145 """
146 Loads distance cache from a JSON file into memory.
147 Inspects cache version silently; a cache file written by a newer version is ignored with a warning, and it is
148 never overwritten by save_distance_cache().
149 """
150 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
151 target_file = str(Path(filepath).resolve()) if filepath is not None else _distance_cache_file
152 if target_file and os.path.isfile(target_file):
153 try:
154 with open(target_file, "r") as f:
155 data = json.load(f)
156 if isinstance(data, dict):
157 cache_ver = data.pop("__version__", None)
158 # If cache is from a future incompatible version, skip loading (and do not overwrite it)
159 if cache_ver is not None and _parse_version(cache_ver) > _parse_version(__version__):
160 _newer_cache_files.add(target_file)
161 sys.stderr.write(
162 f"# Warning: Cache file '{target_file}' has newer version {cache_ver} "
163 f"(current {__version__}); ignoring incompatible cache (the file is not overwritten).\n"
164 )
165 return _distance_cache
166 # Sanitize any legacy CSS cache entries where dmax was set from dmin when dmax_X == dmax_Z == 0
167 for k, v in data.items():
168 if isinstance(v, dict) and k.startswith("css:"):
169 if v.get("dmax_X", 0) == 0 and v.get("dmax_Z", 0) == 0 and "dmax_X" in v:
170 v["dmax"] = 0
171 _distance_cache.update(data)
172 except Exception as e:
173 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: Failed to load distance cache from {target_file}: {e}\n")
174 return _distance_cache
175

177def save_distance_cache(filepath: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None) -> None:
178 """
179 Saves the in-memory distance cache to a JSON file.
180 Silently writes "__version__": __version__ into the file.
181 Uses atomic write via a temporary file to prevent corruption.
182 A cache file written by a newer version (see load_distance_cache()) is not overwritten.
183 """
184 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
185 target_file = str(Path(filepath).resolve()) if filepath is not None else _distance_cache_file
186 if not target_file or target_file in _newer_cache_files:
187 return
188
189 parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(target_file)) or "."
190 os.makedirs(parent_dir, exist_ok=True)
191 fd, temp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".tmp", prefix="dist_cache_", dir=parent_dir)
192 try:
193 cache_data = dict(_distance_cache)
194 cache_data["__version__"] = __version__
195 with open(fd, "w") as f:
196 json.dump(cache_data, f, indent=2)
197 os.replace(temp_path, target_file)
198 except Exception as e:
199 if os.path.exists(temp_path):
200 try: os.remove(temp_path)
201 except OSError: pass
202 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: Failed to save distance cache to {target_file}: {e}\n")
203
204
205def clear_distance_cache(cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None, clear_file: bool = False) -> None:
206 """
207 Clears all cached distance calculations from memory, and optionally deletes the persistent JSON file.
208 """
209 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
210 _distance_cache.clear()
211 target_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
212 if clear_file and target_file and os.path.isfile(target_file):
213 try:
214 os.remove(target_file)
215 _newer_cache_files.discard(target_file)
216 except OSError:
217 pass

238def format_bounds_list(dmin: int, dmax: int, num_rw: int) -> List[int]:
239 """
240 Returns [dmin, dmax, num_rw] according to:
241 - [d, d, 0] if known exactly
242 - [dmin, 0, 0] if there is no upper bound (dmax == 0)
243 - [0, dmax, num_rw] if there is no lower bound (dmin <= 1)
244 - [dmin, dmax, num_rw] otherwise
245 """
246 eff_dmin = dmin if dmin > 1 else 0
247 eff_dmax = dmax if dmax > 0 else 0
248 eff_rw = num_rw if num_rw > 0 else 0
249 if eff_dmin > 0 and eff_dmin == eff_dmax:
250 return [eff_dmin, eff_dmax, 0]
251 elif eff_dmax == 0:
252 return [eff_dmin, 0, 0]
253 elif eff_dmin == 0:
254 return [0, eff_dmax, eff_rw]
255 else:
256 return [eff_dmin, eff_dmax, eff_rw]
257

261 dmin, dmax, num_rw = bounds[0], bounds[1], bounds[2]
262 if dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax:
263 return f"{dmin} {dmax} {num_rw} (exact)"
264 return f"{dmin} {dmax} {num_rw}"

267def rw_infoset_find_prob(n: int, rank: int, w: int, pairs_l: int = 0) -> float:
268 """
269 Information-set estimate of the probability that a RW step finds a given codeword of weight w.
270
271 Model: uniform random information sets (as in the dist_m4ri binary, rw_infoset_find_prob()). A RW step
272 reduces H (rank r) with a random column order; a codeword is found if exactly one of its w positions is among
273 the k = n - r non-pivot columns: P1(w) = w C(n-w, k-1) / C(n, k). Codewords of weight w > r + 1 are never
274 found (P1 = 0). With the RW pairs (pairs_l > 0, the binary's option pairs), also if exactly two of its positions
275 are non-pivot columns and its other w - 2 positions avoid the l pivot rows of the buckets:
276 P2(w) = C(w, 2) C(n-w, k-2) / C(n, k) * C(r - w + 2, l) / C(r, l), and the probability is P1 + P2.
277
278 Args:
279 n: Block length (number of columns of H).
280 rank: Rank r of H.
281 w: Codeword weight.
282 pairs_l: The number l of pivot rows of the buckets of the RW pairs (0: no pairs).
283
284 Returns:
285 P1(w) + P2(w).
286 """
287 import math
288 k = n - rank
289 if n <= 0 or rank < 0 or k <= 0 or w < 1 or w > n or w - 1 > rank:
290 return 0.0
291
292 def log_binom(a: int, b: int) -> float:
293 return math.lgamma(a + 1) - math.lgamma(b + 1) - math.lgamma(a - b + 1)
294
295 p = math.exp(math.log(w) + log_binom(n - w, k - 1) - log_binom(n, k))
296 if pairs_l > 0 and w >= 2 and k >= 2 and w - 2 + pairs_l <= rank:
297 p += math.exp(log_binom(w, 2) + log_binom(n - w, k - 2) - log_binom(n, k) + log_binom(rank - w + 2, pairs_l)
298 - log_binom(rank, pairs_l))
299 return min(1.0, p)
300
301
302def rw_infoset_estimate(
303 n: int, rank: int, steps: int, d: int, dmin: int = 1, step_time: float = 0.0, target: float = 0.01,
304 steps_total: int = 0, pairs_l: int = 0
305) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
306 """
307 Information-set estimate of the probability that RW missed a codeword lighter than the upper bound d found.
308
309 Among the weights max(dmin, 1) <= w < d (not excluded by CC), the weight hardest to find (the smallest P(w),
310 see rw_infoset_find_prob()) is used: a single codeword of this weight is missed in `steps` RW steps with uniform
311 random permutations with probability (1 - P)^steps. The number of RW steps for the target miss probability is
312 given in total, with the fraction steps / steps_total of uniform steps as in the run (localized windows, used in
313 about half of the steps for n >= 500, are not counted). Same as print_rw_infoset_estimate() in the binary.
314
315 Args:
316 n: Block length (number of columns of H).
317 rank: Rank of H.
318 steps: Number of completed RW steps with uniform random permutations.
319 d: Smallest weight found (the upper bound dmax).
320 dmin: Certified lower bound (smaller weights are excluded).
321 step_time: Wall time per RW step in seconds (0: unknown).
322 target: Target miss probability (default: 0.01).
323 steps_total: Number of all completed RW steps (0: the same as `steps`).
324 pairs_l: The number l of pivot rows of the buckets of the RW pairs (0: no pairs), see rw_infoset_find_prob().
325
326 Returns:
327 Dictionary with the weight `w`, the probability `p_find` = P(w) per step, the miss probability `p_miss`,
328 the total number of RW steps `steps_target` for the target miss probability (None if the codeword cannot be
329 found), and the corresponding wall time `time_target` (None if unknown); or None if there are no weights to
330 check.
331 """
332 import math
333 w_lo, w_hi = max(dmin, 1), d - 1
334 if w_hi < w_lo or n <= 0:
335 return None
336 w_hard, p1 = w_hi, rw_infoset_find_prob(n, rank, w_hi, pairs_l) # the weight hardest to find (smallest P)
337 for w in range(w_lo, w_hi):
338 pw = rw_infoset_find_prob(n, rank, w, pairs_l)
339 if pw < p1:
340 w_hard, p1 = w, pw
341 steps_target: Optional[int]
342 if p1 <= 0.0:
343 p_miss, steps_target = 1.0, None
344 elif p1 >= 1.0:
345 p_miss, steps_target = (0.0 if steps > 0 else 1.0), 1
346 else:
347 lq = math.log1p(-p1)
348 p_miss = math.exp(steps * lq) if steps > 0 else 1.0
349 steps_target = math.ceil(math.log(target) / lq)
350 if steps_target is not None and steps > 0 and steps_total > steps:
351 steps_target = math.ceil(steps_target * steps_total / steps)
352 time_target = steps_target * step_time if (steps_target is not None and step_time > 0.0) else None
353 return {"w": w_hard, "p_find": p1, "p_miss": p_miss, "steps_target": steps_target, "time_target": time_target}
354

356def _format_duration(t: float) -> str:
357 """Formats a duration in seconds (s, min, h, or days), as in the dist_m4ri binary."""
358 if t < 120.0:
359 return f"{t:.3g} s"
360 if t < 7200.0:
361 return f"{t / 60.0:.3g} min"
362 if t < 172800.0:
363 return f"{t / 3600.0:.3g} h"
364 return f"{t / 86400.0:.3g} days"

367def _parse_stderr_stats(stderr: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
368 """Parses codeword and hit statistics from dist_m4ri stderr output."""
369 import re
370 stats: Dict[str, Any] = {"extra_weights": [], "rw_converged": False, "hit_warnings": []}
371 if not stderr:
372 return stats
373 hit_warning: Optional[List[str]] = None
374 skip_estimate = False
375 for line in stderr.splitlines():
376 line_s = line.strip()
377 if line_s.startswith("# information-set estimate"): # printed by the binary after a hit warning
378 skip_estimate = True
379 elif skip_estimate and line_s.startswith("# "):
380 continue
381 else:
382 skip_estimate = False
383 if skip_estimate:
384 if hit_warning is not None:
385 stats["hit_warnings"].append(" ".join(hit_warning))
386 hit_warning = None
387 continue
388 if hit_warning is not None:
389 if line_s.startswith("# "): # continuation of a hit uniformity warning
390 hit_warning.append(line_s[1:].strip())
391 continue
392 stats["hit_warnings"].append(" ".join(hit_warning))
393 hit_warning = None
394 if line_s.startswith("# Warning: non-uniform RW hit counts"):
395 hit_warning = [line_s[len("# Warning: "):]]
396 continue
397 if line_s.startswith("# Note: drop=") and " not used: " in line_s: # the reduction (drop=FILE) is not exact
398 stats["drop_note"] = line_s.split(" not used: ", 1)[1].replace("; using the full DEM", "")
399 continue
400 if line_s.startswith("# Note: drop=") and "none of the listed detectors is in the DEM" in line_s:
401 stats["drop_none_listed"] = True
402 continue
403 if line_s.startswith("# RW information sets:"):
404 m_rw = re.search(
405 r"n=(\d+), rank\‍(H\‍)=(\d+), steps=(\d+) \‍(uniform permutations: (\d+)\‍), ksub=(\d+), "
406 r"(?:pairs=(\d+), )?([0-9.eE+-]+) s/step per thread, (\d+) RW threads", line_s
407 )
408 if m_rw:
409 stats["rw_n"] = int(m_rw.group(1))
410 stats["rw_rank"] = int(m_rw.group(2))
411 stats["rw_steps"] = int(m_rw.group(3))
412 stats["rw_steps_uniform"] = int(m_rw.group(4))
413 stats["rw_ksub"] = int(m_rw.group(5))
414 stats["rw_pairs_l"] = int(m_rw.group(6)) if m_rw.group(6) else 0
415 stats["rw_step_time"] = float(m_rw.group(7))
416 stats["rw_threads"] = int(m_rw.group(8))
417 continue
418 if line_s.startswith("# RW pairs (p=2"): # the pairs checked, and the codewords found by pairs and singles
419 m_p = re.search(r"([0-9.eE+-]+) pairs checked per step; .*: (\d+) from pairs, (\d+) from single columns",
420 line_s)
421 if m_p:
422 stats["rw_pairs_per_step"] = float(m_p.group(1))
423 stats["rw_hits_pairs"] = int(m_p.group(2))
424 stats["rw_hits_single"] = int(m_p.group(3))
425 continue
426 if line_s.startswith("# RW step types, w="): # the codewords found by the uniform and by the window steps
427 m_st = re.search(r"w=(\d+): uniform steps: cws=(\d+), hits=(\d+); window steps: cws=(\d+), hits=(\d+); "
428 r"both: cws=(\d+) \‍(of (\d+) cws\‍)", line_s)
429 if m_st:
430 v = [int(x) for x in m_st.groups()]
431 stats.setdefault("rw_step_types", {})[v[0]] = {
432 "uniform_cws": v[1], "uniform_hits": v[2], "window_cws": v[3], "window_hits": v[4],
433 "both_cws": v[5], "cws": v[6]}
434 continue
435 if line_s.startswith("# rounds of the DEM:"): # the input summary (debug & 1, a DEM)
436 m_r = re.search(r"D=(\d+) detectors and L=(\d+) columns per round \‍(estimated: score ([0-9.]+)\‍)", line_s)
437 m_n = re.search(r"best score ([0-9.]+)", line_s)
438 if m_r:
439 stats["rounds"] = {"D": int(m_r.group(1)), "L": int(m_r.group(2)), "score": float(m_r.group(3))}
440 elif m_n:
441 stats["rounds"] = {"D": 0, "L": 0, "score": float(m_n.group(1))}
442 continue
443 if "RW convergence reached" in line_s: # progress line (debug & 2) or the stop reason (debug & 1)
444 stats["rw_converged"] = True
445 if line_s.startswith("# codewords accumulated: total=0"):
446 stats["total_cws"] = 0
447 elif line_s.startswith("# codewords accumulated:"):
448 m = re.search(
449 r"total=(\d+),\s*min_w=(\d+):\s*cws=(\d+),\s*total_hits=(\d+),\s*"
450 r"hits min=(\d+),\s*max=(\d+),\s*avg=([0-9.]+),\s*stdev=([0-9.]+)",
451 line_s
452 )
453 if m:
454 stats["total_cws"] = int(m.group(1))
455 stats["min_w"] = int(m.group(2))
456 stats["cws"] = int(m.group(3))
457 stats["total_hits"] = int(m.group(4))
458 stats["hits_min"] = int(m.group(5))
459 stats["hits_max"] = int(m.group(6))
460 stats["hits_avg"] = float(m.group(7))
461 stats["hits_stdev"] = float(m.group(8))
462 m_set = re.search(
463 r"<n>=([0-9.]+) over (\d+) cws of w=(\d+)\.\.(\d+) \‍(min_hits=(\d+), cov_cws=(-?\d+)\‍)", line_s
464 )
465 if m_set:
466 stats["avg_hits"] = float(m_set.group(1))
467 stats["set_cws"] = int(m_set.group(2))
468 stats["set_w_lo"] = int(m_set.group(3))
469 stats["set_w_hi"] = int(m_set.group(4))
470 stats["min_hits"] = int(m_set.group(5))
471 stats["cov_cws"] = int(m_set.group(6))
472 elif line_s.startswith("# codewords w="):
473 m_w = re.search(
474 r"w=(\d+):\s*cws=(\d+),\s*total_hits=(\d+),\s*"
475 r"hits min=(\d+),\s*max=(\d+),\s*avg=([0-9.]+),\s*stdev=([0-9.]+)",
476 line_s
477 )
478 if m_w:
479 stats["extra_weights"].append({
480 "w": int(m_w.group(1)),
481 "cws": int(m_w.group(2)),
482 "total_hits": int(m_w.group(3)),
483 "hits_min": int(m_w.group(4)),
484 "hits_max": int(m_w.group(5)),
485 "hits_avg": float(m_w.group(6)),
486 "hits_stdev": float(m_w.group(7)),
487 })
488 if hit_warning is not None:
489 stats["hit_warnings"].append(" ".join(hit_warning))
490 return stats

493def explain_bounds(
494 bounds: List[int],
495 method: Optional[int] = None,
496 label: str = "",
497 stats: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
498 dstop: int = 0
499) -> str:
500 """
501 Returns a human-readable explanation of [dmin, dmax, num_rw] following README.md.
502
503 Args:
504 bounds: [dmin, dmax, rw_steps] list.
505 method: Optional solver method (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing).
506 label: Optional prefix/label (e.g. "dX", "dZ", "").
507 stats: Optional dictionary of codeword and hit statistics parsed from dist_m4ri.
508 dstop: Stop target of the search (0: none); once dmin >= dstop, the upper bound is not needed, and the
509 estimates of the probability that RW missed a lighter codeword are skipped.
510
511 Returns:
512 Multi-line formatted explanation string.
513 """
514 dmin, dmax, num_rw = bounds[0], bounds[1], bounds[2]
515 lines = []
516 prefix = f"{label} " if label else ""
517 stopped = dstop > 0 and dmin >= dstop and not (dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax)
518
519 # Lower bound explanation
520 if dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax:
521 lines.append(f" {prefix}Lower bound (dmin = {dmin}): Exact distance certified (dmin == dmax == {dmin}).")
522 elif dmin > 1:
523 lines.append(f" {prefix}Lower bound (dmin = {dmin}): All cluster weights w <= {dmin - 1} "
524 f"were exhaustively analyzed by CC without finding any non-trivial codewords.")
525 else:
526 lines.append(f" {prefix}Lower bound (dmin = {dmin}): No non-trivial lower bound certified (dmin <= 1).")
527
528 # Upper bound explanation
529 if dmax > 0:
530 lines.append(f" {prefix}Upper bound (dmax = {dmax}): Weight of the smallest non-trivial codeword discovered.")
531 else:
532 lines.append(f" {prefix}Upper bound (dmax = {dmax}): No non-trivial codeword discovered yet (dmax = 0).")
533 if stopped:
534 lines.append(f" {prefix}Stop target (dstop = {dstop}): reached, the search ended once dmin >= {dstop} was "
535 f"certified (no codeword of weight < {dstop}); the upper bound is not needed.")
536
537 # RW steps explanation (and why it is zero if num_rw == 0)
538 if num_rw > 0:
539 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = {num_rw}): {num_rw} completed random "
540 f"information set searches across worker threads.")
541 else:
542 if dmin > 0 and dmin == dmax:
543 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = 0): Set to 0 because the exact distance "
544 f"d = {dmin} was proven by Connected Cluster search or certified bounds coincided.")
545 elif method == 2:
546 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = 0): Set to 0 because Method 2 (Connected Cluster) "
547 f"is an exhaustive search that does not perform random information set (RW) sampling.")
548 else:
549 lines.append(f" {prefix}Random window steps (rw_steps = 0): 0 completed random information set steps.")
550
551 if stats and "total_cws" in stats:
552 if stats["total_cws"] > 0:
553 lines.append(
554 f" {prefix}Codewords accumulated: {stats['total_cws']} distinct "
555 f"(w = {stats['min_w']}: {stats['cws']} codewords, {stats['total_hits']} total hits; "
556 f"hits min = {stats['hits_min']}, max = {stats['hits_max']}, "
557 f"avg = {stats['hits_avg']:.2f}, stdev = {stats['hits_stdev']:.2f})."
558 )
559 if stats.get("min_hits", 0) > 0 and "avg_hits" in stats:
560 import math
561 conv_str = "CONVERGED" if stats.get("rw_converged") else "not converged"
562 lines.append(
563 f" {prefix}Hit convergence (min_hits = {stats['min_hits']}, "
564 f"cov_cws = {stats['cov_cws']}): <n> = {stats['avg_hits']:.2f} average hits per codeword "
565 f"({stats['set_cws']} codewords of weight {stats['set_w_lo']}..{stats['set_w_hi']}), "
566 f"P_fail ~ exp(-<n>) = {math.exp(-stats['avg_hits']):.2g} ({conv_str})."
567 )
568 for ew in stats.get("extra_weights", []):
569 lines.append(
570 f" {prefix}Codewords (w = {ew['w']}): {ew['cws']} codewords, "
571 f"{ew['total_hits']} total hits; hits min = {ew['hits_min']}, "
572 f"max = {ew['hits_max']}, avg = {ew['hits_avg']:.2f}, "
573 f"stdev = {ew['hits_stdev']:.2f}."
574 )
575 n_all, n_unif = stats.get("rw_steps", 0), stats.get("rw_steps_uniform", 0)
576 for w, st in sorted(stats.get("rw_step_types", {}).items()):
577 lines.append(
578 f" {prefix}Codewords (w = {w}) by RW step type: {st['uniform_cws']} found in the {n_unif} uniform "
579 f"steps ({st['uniform_hits']} hits), {st['window_cws']} in the {n_all - n_unif} window steps "
580 f"({st['window_hits']} hits), {st['both_cws']} in both (of {st['cws']} codewords)."
581 )
582 if stats.get("rw_pairs_l", 0) > 0 and "rw_pairs_per_step" in stats:
583 lines.append(
584 f" {prefix}RW pairs (p=2, buckets of l = {stats['rw_pairs_l']} pivot rows): "
585 f"{stats['rw_pairs_per_step']:.3g} pairs checked per RW step; codewords recorded with weight up to "
586 f"the upper bound: {stats['rw_hits_pairs']} from pairs, {stats['rw_hits_single']} from single "
587 f"columns."
588 )
589 for hw in stats.get("hit_warnings", []):
590 lines.append(f" {prefix}WARNING: {hw}")
591 else:
592 lines.append(f" {prefix}Codewords accumulated: 0 distinct non-trivial codewords found.")
593
594 # The RW upper bound is not certified: estimated probability that RW missed a lighter codeword
595 if stats and num_rw > 0 and dmax > max(dmin, 1) and not stopped:
596 import math
597 rw_threads = stats.get("rw_threads", 0)
598 step_wall = stats.get("rw_step_time", 0.0) / rw_threads if rw_threads > 0 else 0.0
599 avg = stats.get("avg_hits", 0.0)
600 if stats.get("min_hits", 0) > 0 and avg > 0.0:
601 p_hit = math.exp(-avg)
602 if p_hit > 0.01:
603 need = math.ceil(num_rw * math.log(100.0) / avg) # the average number of hits grows with the steps
604 t_str = f", ~{_format_duration((need - num_rw) * step_wall)} more" if step_wall > 0.0 else ""
605 lines.append(f" {prefix}Hit-based estimate: P_fail ~ exp(-<n>) = {p_hit:.2g}; 1% after about {need} "
606 f"RW steps in total{t_str}.")
607 else:
608 lines.append(f" {prefix}Hit-based estimate: P_fail ~ exp(-<n>) = {p_hit:.2g} (below 1%).")
609 n_unif = stats.get("rw_steps_uniform", 0)
610 if stats.get("rw_n", 0) > 0 and stats.get("rw_ksub", 0) == 0 and n_unif > 0:
611 n_cols, rank = stats["rw_n"], stats["rw_rank"]
612 pairs_l = stats.get("rw_pairs_l", 0)
613 est = rw_infoset_estimate(n_cols, rank, n_unif, dmax, dmin=max(dmin, 1), step_time=step_wall,
614 steps_total=stats.get("rw_steps", n_unif), pairs_l=pairs_l)
615 if est is not None and est["steps_target"] is None:
616 lines.append(f" {prefix}Information-set estimate: a codeword of weight {est['w']} cannot be found "
617 f"by RW (n = {n_cols}, rank(H) = {rank}).")
618 elif est is not None:
619 t_str = (f", ~{_format_duration(est['time_target'])}" if est["time_target"] is not None else "")
620 p_str = f" with pairs, l = {pairs_l}" if pairs_l > 0 else ""
621 lines.append(
622 f" {prefix}Information-set estimate (uniform random information sets{p_str}; n = {n_cols}, "
623 f"rank(H) = {rank}, {n_unif} of {stats.get('rw_steps', n_unif)} RW steps uniform): a single "
624 f"codeword of weight {est['w']} < {dmax} is found with probability {est['p_find']:.3g} per RW "
625 f"step and would be missed with probability {est['p_miss']:.2g}; 1% after about "
626 f"{est['steps_target']} RW steps in total{t_str}."
627 )
628 if stats.get("min_w") == dmax and "hits_avg" in stats:
629 n_all = stats.get("rw_steps", n_unif)
630 p1 = rw_infoset_find_prob(n_cols, rank, dmax, pairs_l)
631 st = stats.get("rw_step_types", {}).get(dmax)
632 if st is not None and st["cws"] > 0: # the hits of the uniform steps only
633 n_ref, obs, note = n_unif, st["uniform_hits"] / st["cws"], " in the uniform steps"
634 else:
635 n_ref, obs = n_all, stats["hits_avg"]
636 note = "" if n_unif == n_all else ", including the steps with localized windows"
637 exp_hits = n_ref * p1
638 verdict = ("the uniform model is conservative here" if obs >= exp_hits else
639 "codewords are found less often than in the uniform model, the information-set "
640 "estimate may be optimistic")
641 lines.append(
642 f" {prefix}Model check: expected hits per codeword of weight {dmax} in {n_ref} uniform RW "
643 f"steps: {exp_hits:.3g}, observed average {obs:.2f}{note} ({verdict})."
644 )
645 elif stats.get("rw_n", 0) > 0:
646 lines.append(f" {prefix}Information-set estimate: not available (ksub > 0 or kwin > 0: no uniform "
647 f"random information sets).")
648
649 return "\n".join(lines)
650

652def get_cached_distance(
653 H: Optional[Any] = None,
654 G: Optional[Any] = None,
655 L: Optional[Any] = None,
656 Hx: Optional[Any] = None,
657 Hz: Optional[Any] = None,
658 Lx: Optional[Any] = None,
659 Lz: Optional[Any] = None,
660 dem: Optional[Any] = None,
661 circuit: Optional[Any] = None,
662 pmin: float = 0.0,
663 cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
664 start: Optional[Union[int, str, Sequence[int]]] = None,
665 simple: Optional[bool] = None,
666 full: Optional[bool] = None,
667 basis: Optional[str] = None,
668 rounds: Optional[int] = None,
669 p_noise: float = 0.001,
670 force_noise: bool = False
671) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
672 """
673 Retrieves the cached distance entry (including bounds and cumulative rw_steps)
674 for a given code matrix, CSS code, or DEM.
675
676 If the expert CC start-column list `start` is given (see compute_classical_distance), the
677 separate start-list record (cache key suffix ':start=a,b,c') is returned instead of the main record.
678
679 For a CSS code (Hx and Hz, optionally Lx / Lz), the entry is assembled from the records of its two sectors,
680 the quantum codes (H=Hx, G=Hz) -> dZ and (H=Hz, G=Hx) -> dX (shared with compute_quantum_distance()): the fields
681 dmin_X, dmax_X, rw_steps_X, dX, cws_X (the same for Z), and dist, dmin, dmax, rw_steps of d = min(dX, dZ).
682
683 For a Stim circuit (circuit, or dem with a .stim file), the cache key is that of the DEM processed as in
684 compute_dem_distance(), with the same options rounds, p_noise, and force_noise (simple and full are disabled since
685 version 0.13.0: ignored with a warning to stderr; basis does not change the DEM).
686
687 Returns:
688 dict with keys {"dist", "dmin", "dmax", "rw_steps", ...} or None if not cached.
689 """
690 global _distance_cache, _distance_cache_file
691 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
692 if eff_cache_file:
693 load_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
694 sfx = _start_key_suffix(_normalize_start_list(start))
695
696 if H is not None:
697 entry = _distance_cache.get(_matrix_cache_key(H, G, L, classical=(G is None and L is None)) + sfx)
698 if entry:
699 entry = dict(entry)
700 entry["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(entry.get("dmin", 0), entry.get("dmax", 0), entry.get("rw_steps", 0))
701 return entry
702 elif Hx is not None or Hz is not None:
703 # a CSS code is cached as its two sectors (H=Hx, G=Hz) -> dZ and (H=Hz, G=Hx) -> dX, see compute_css_distance()
704 if Hx is None or Hz is None:
705 return None
706 _migrate_css_records(Hx, Hz, Lx, Lz, eff_cache_file)
707 codes = _css_sector_codes(Hx, Hz, Lx, Lz)
708 sec = {s: _distance_cache.get(_matrix_cache_key(*codes[s]) + sfx) for s in ("X", "Z")}
709 if not sec["X"] and not sec["Z"]:
710 return None
711 entry = {}
712 bounds = {}
713 for s in ("X", "Z"):
714 rec = sec[s] or {}
715 b = (rec.get("dmin", 0) or 0, rec.get("dmax", 0) or 0, rec.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0)
716 bounds[s] = b
717 entry[f"dmin_{s}"], entry[f"dmax_{s}"], entry[f"rw_steps_{s}"] = b
718 entry[f"d{s}"] = format_bounds_list(*b)
719 entry[f"cws_{s}"] = list(rec.get("cws", []))
720 dist, d_lo, d_hi, rw = _css_combine(bounds["X"], bounds["Z"])
721 entry.update({"dist": dist, "dmin": d_lo, "dmax": d_hi, "rw_steps": rw})
722 return entry
723 elif dem is not None or circuit is not None:
724 # the key of compute_dem_distance(): a Stim circuit is processed and converted in the same way
725 _warn_disabled_simple_full(simple, full)
726 dem_obj, _, _ = _dem_from_input(dem, circuit, basis=basis, rounds=rounds, p_noise=p_noise,
727 force_noise=force_noise)
728 entry = _distance_cache.get(_dem_cache_key(dem_obj, pmin) + sfx)
729 if entry:
730 entry = dict(entry)
731 entry["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(entry.get("dmin", 0), entry.get("dmax", 0), entry.get("rw_steps", 0))
732 return entry
733 return None
734
735
736# Backward-compatibility aliases
737clear_css_distance_cache = clear_distance_cache
738enable_css_distance_cache = enable_distance_cache
739disable_css_distance_cache = disable_distance_cache
740

742def get_sparse_array_state(A) -> str:
743 """Returns a deterministic string representation for JSON-compatible cache keys."""
744 if A is None:
745 return "none"
746 if isinstance(A, (str, Path)):
747 path_str = str(Path(A).resolve())
748 if os.path.isfile(path_str):
749 try:
750 with open(path_str, "rb") as f:
751 content_h = hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()
752 return f"file:{path_str}:{content_h}"
753 except Exception:
754 return f"file:{path_str}"
755 return path_str
756 if hasattr(A, 'shape') and hasattr(A, 'dtype') and hasattr(A, 'tobytes'):
757 h = hashlib.sha256(A.tobytes()).hexdigest()
758 dtype_str = getattr(A.dtype, 'str', str(A.dtype))
759 return f"ndarray:{A.shape}:{dtype_str}:{h}"
760 if hasattr(A, 'tocsr'):
761 csr = A.tocsr()
762 h = hashlib.sha256(csr.data.tobytes() + csr.indices.tobytes() + csr.indptr.tobytes()).hexdigest()
763 return f"csr:{csr.shape}:{h}"
764 if hasattr(A, 'tobytes'):
765 h = hashlib.sha256(A.tobytes()).hexdigest()
766 return f"bytes:{h}"
767 h = hashlib.sha256(str(A).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
768 return f"str_sha256:{h}"
769

771def create_unique_file(directory: Union[str, Path] = "tmp", extension: str = ".tmp") -> str:
772 """Creates a unique temporary file path and ensures the parent directory exists."""
773 try:
774 os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
775 fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=extension, dir=directory)
776 except OSError:
777 fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=extension)
778 os.close(fd)
779 return path

782def _remove_temp_files(files: Sequence[Optional[str]], debug: int = 0) -> None:
783 """Removes the temporary files `files` (None entries are skipped); with the debug bit PY_DBG_KEEP_FILES, the
784 files are kept and listed instead."""
785 for f in files:
786 if not f or not os.path.exists(f):
787 continue
788 if debug & PY_DBG_KEEP_FILES:
789 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Kept temporary file: {f}")
790 continue
791 try:
792 os.remove(f)
793 except OSError:
794 pass

797def read_sparse_vectors(filepath: str) -> List[List[int]]:
798 """
799 Reads a list of sparse vectors from a text file in NZLIST format,
800 converting from 1-based indexing (in the file) to 0-based indexing (in Python).
801
802 Args:
803 filepath (str): The path to the text file.
804
805 Returns:
806 list of list of int: A list where each element is a 0-based sparse vector.
807 """
808 sparse_vectors = []
809 if not os.path.exists(filepath) or os.path.getsize(filepath) == 0:
810 return sparse_vectors
811
812 with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
813 first_line = f.readline().strip()
814 if not first_line:
815 return sparse_vectors
816 if first_line != '%% NZLIST':
817 raise ValueError(f"Invalid file format in {filepath}: Missing '%% NZLIST' header.")
818
819 for line_num, line in enumerate(f, start=2):
820 line = line.strip()
821 if not line or line.startswith('%'):
822 continue
823 try:
824 parts = list(map(int, line.split()))
825 except ValueError:
826 raise ValueError(f"Non-integer data found on line {line_num}: {line}")
827
828 stated_length = parts[0]
829 vector_elements = [x - 1 for x in parts[1:]]
830 if len(vector_elements) != stated_length:
831 raise ValueError(
832 f"Length mismatch on line {line_num}. "
833 f"Expected {stated_length} elements, but found {len(vector_elements)}."
834 )
835 sparse_vectors.append(vector_elements)
836
837 return sparse_vectors
838

840def find_dist_m4ri_binary(custom_path: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
841 """Finds the dist_m4ri executable."""
842 if custom_path:
843 if os.path.isfile(custom_path) and os.access(custom_path, os.X_OK):
844 return os.path.abspath(custom_path)
845 raise FileNotFoundError(
846 f"Specified executable '{custom_path}' not found or not executable."
847 )
848
849 pkg_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
850 candidates = [
851 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "src", "dist_m4ri"),
852 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "dist_m4ri"),
853 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "bin", "dist_m4ri"),
854 os.path.join(pkg_dir, "..", "dist-m4ri", "src", "dist_m4ri"),
855 os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "src", "dist_m4ri"),
856 os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "dist_m4ri"),
857 os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "bin", "dist_m4ri"),
858 ]
859
860 for cand in candidates:
861 if os.path.isfile(cand) and os.access(cand, os.X_OK):
862 return os.path.abspath(cand)
863
864 which_path = shutil.which("dist_m4ri")
865 if which_path:
866 return which_path
867
868 raise FileNotFoundError(
869 "Could not find executable 'dist_m4ri'. Please run 'make -C src' to build it."
870 )
871

873def _parse_version(v_str: str) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
874 import re
875 parts = re.findall(r"\d+", v_str)
876 return tuple(int(p) for p in parts) if parts else (0,)
877
878
879def _binary_version(binary_path: Optional[str] = None) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str], Optional[str]]:
880 """
881 The dist_m4ri binary and its version (from `dist_m4ri --version`).
882
883 Returns:
884 (path, version, error): path is None if the binary is not found; version is None if it is unknown (then
885 error is the reason, or None if the binary does not support --version).
886 """
887 try:
888 path = find_dist_m4ri_binary(binary_path)
889 except (RuntimeError, FileNotFoundError):
890 return None, None, None
891 try:
892 proc = subprocess.run([path, "--version"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
893 timeout=2.0)
894 except Exception as e:
895 return path, None, str(e)
896 if proc.returncode == 0 and "version" in proc.stdout:
897 return path, proc.stdout.strip().split()[-1], None
898 return path, None, None
899
900
901def check_binary_compatibility(binary_path: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
902 """
903 Checks if the backend dist_m4ri binary exists and is compatible (version >= __version__).
904 Returns a warning message string if missing or older, or None if compatible (silent).
905 """
906 path, bin_ver, error = _binary_version(binary_path)
907 if path is None:
908 return "Warning: backend binary 'dist_m4ri' not found (run 'make -C src' to build it)"
909 if error is not None:
910 return f"Warning: failed to check binary '{path}': {error}"
911 if bin_ver is None:
912 return (
913 f"Warning: backend binary '{path}' does not support --version "
914 f"(expected >= {__version__}; run 'make -C src' to rebuild)"
915 )
916 if _parse_version(bin_ver) < _parse_version(__version__):
917 return (
918 f"Warning: backend binary '{path}' is version {bin_ver} "
919 f"(expected >= {__version__}; run 'make -C src' to rebuild)"
920 )
921 return None # Compatible and up-to-date: silent!
922
923
924def parse_dist_m4ri_output(stdout: str) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
925 """
926 Parses the standard output of dist_m4ri.
927 Expected format on stdout: "dmin dmax rw_steps", "dmin dmax", or a single integer.
928
929 Returns:
930 tuple (dmin, dmax, rw_steps)
931 """
932 lines = stdout.strip().split('\n')
933 for line in reversed(lines):
934 line = line.strip()
935 if not line or line.startswith('#'):
936 continue
937 parts = line.split()
938 if len(parts) >= 3:
939 try:
940 return int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
941 except ValueError:
942 continue
943 elif len(parts) == 2:
944 try:
945 return int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), 0
946 except ValueError:
947 continue
948 elif len(parts) == 1:
949 try:
950 val = int(parts[0])
951 return val, val, 0
952 except ValueError:
953 continue
954
955 raise RuntimeError(f"Could not parse dist_m4ri output: {stdout}")
956
957
958class DistanceResult:
959 """
960 Structured result for code distance calculations containing:
961 - dmin: lower bound on distance
962 - dmax: upper bound on distance (minimum non-trivial codeword weight found)
963 - rw_steps: cumulative number of completed random window information sets
964 - cws: discovered codewords (if requested)
965 """
966 def __init__(
967 self,
968 dmin: int,
969 dmax: int,
970 rw_steps: int = 0,
971 cws: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None,
972 cws_X: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None,
973 cws_Z: Optional[List[List[int]]] = None,
974 dmin_X: Optional[int] = None,
975 dmax_X: Optional[int] = None,
976 rw_steps_X: Optional[int] = None,
977 dmin_Z: Optional[int] = None,
978 dmax_Z: Optional[int] = None,
979 rw_steps_Z: Optional[int] = None,
980 ):
981 self.dmin = dmin
982 self.dmax = dmax
983 self.rw_steps = rw_steps
984 self.cws = cws
985 self.cws_X = cws_X
986 self.cws_Z = cws_Z
987 self.dmin_X = dmin_X
988 self.dmax_X = dmax_X
989 self.rw_steps_X = rw_steps_X
990 self.dmin_Z = dmin_Z
991 self.dmax_Z = dmax_Z
992 self.rw_steps_Z = rw_steps_Z
993
994 @property
995 def is_exact(self) -> bool:
996 return self.dmin > 0 and self.dmin == self.dmax
997
998 @property
999 def dist(self) -> int:
1000 return self.dmin if self.is_exact else (self.dmax if self.dmax > 0 else self.dmin)
1001
1002 def __int__(self) -> int:
1003 return self.distdist
1004
1005 def __index__(self) -> int:
1006 return self.distdist
1007
1008 def __eq__(self, other: Any) -> bool:
1009 if isinstance(other, DistanceResult):
1010 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps) == (other.dmin, other.dmax, other.rw_steps)
1011 if isinstance(other, (tuple, list)):
1012 return self._fields() == tuple(other)
1013 if isinstance(other, numbers.Integral): # int, bool, and numpy integers
1014 return self.distdist == other
1015 return False
1016
1017 def _fields(self) -> tuple:
1018 """The result as a tuple (dmin, dmax, rw_steps[, cws] or [, cws_X, cws_Z])."""
1019 if self.cws_X is not None or self.cws_Z is not None:
1020 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps, self.cws_X or [], self.cws_Z or [])
1021 if self.cws is not None:
1022 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps, self.cws)
1023 return (self.dmin, self.dmax, self.rw_steps)
1024
1025 def __iter__(self):
1026 return iter(self._fields())
1027
1028 def __getitem__(self, index: int):
1029 return self._fields()[index]
1030
1031 def __len__(self) -> int: # (not len(tuple(self)): tuple() calls __len__)
1032 return len(self._fields())
1033
1034 def __str__(self) -> str:
1035 if self.is_exact:
1036 return f"{self.dmin} {self.dmax} {self.rw_steps} (exact)"
1037 return f"{self.dmin} {self.dmax} {self.rw_steps}"
1038
1039 def __repr__(self) -> str:
1040 if self.is_exact:
1041 return f"DistanceResult({self.dmin} {self.dmax} {self.rw_steps} (exact))"
1042 return f"DistanceResult(dmin={self.dmin}, dmax={self.dmax}, rw_steps={self.rw_steps})"
1043
1044
1045def check_finc_outc(finC: Optional[str], outC: Optional[str], verbose: bool = False) -> Optional[str]:
1046 """
1047 When finC and outC names are identical, an empty or non-existent file is silently ignored
1048 (with a warning if verbose is True).
1049
1050 Returns:
1051 The effective finC filepath to use (or None if ignored).
1052 """
1053 if not finC:
1054 return None
1055 if outC and (finC == outC or os.path.abspath(finC) == os.path.abspath(outC)):
1056 if not os.path.exists(finC) or os.path.getsize(finC) == 0:
1057 if verbose:
1058 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Warning: finC='{finC}' (identical to outC) is empty or non-existent; "
1059 f"silently ignoring input codewords.")
1060 return None
1061 return finC
1062
1063
1064# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1065# Expert CC options: `start` list of CC start columns, `trust_start`, and the disabled options noscan, cbeg, cend.
1066#
1067# - start=a,b,c: CC clusters are grown only from the listed columns, and they are NOT limited to larger column
1068# indices (unlike cbeg/cend in the dist_m4ri binary). The lower bound dmin (and an exact result) is valid only
1069# if a code symmetry maps every codeword to one whose support contains a listed column (e.g., one column per
1070# block of a quasi-cyclic code); the upper bound dmax is always valid. Results are cached under the separate
1071# key '<key>:start=a,b,c' (sorted, distinct columns). Only dmax and the codewords are merged into the main
1072# record, unless the expert option trust_start is set (then dmin and rw_steps are merged as well, and an
1073# existing exact start-list record is copied to the main record even if no calculation is needed).
1074# - noscan, cbeg, cend: disabled in the Python interface (ignored with a warning to stderr); use the dist_m4ri
1075# binary directly (noscan: CC only at w=wmax; cbeg/cend: start-column range for split multi-run use, where
1076# each column is eventually listed in one of the runs).
1077# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1078
1079def _normalize_start_list(start: Any) -> Optional[List[int]]:
1080 """
1081 Normalizes the expert CC start-column specification `start` into a sorted list of distinct
1082 non-negative (0-based) column indices, or None if unset.
1083
1084 Accepts None, an integer, a comma-separated string (e.g., "0,48"), or a sequence of integers.
1085 A single negative value (e.g., -1, the default of the dist_m4ri binary) means unset (all columns).
1086
1087 Raises:
1088 ValueError: on malformed input or on negative entries in a list of several columns.
1089 """
1090 import operator
1091 if start is None:
1092 return None
1093 err_msg = f"invalid start={start!r}: expected a comma-separated list of column indices, e.g., start=0,48"
1094 vals: List[int] = []
1095 if isinstance(start, str):
1096 s = start.strip()
1097 if not s:
1098 return None
1099 try:
1100 vals = [int(tok) for tok in s.split(",")]
1101 except ValueError:
1102 raise ValueError(err_msg) from None
1103 else:
1104 try:
1105 items = list(start)
1106 except TypeError:
1107 items = [start]
1108 for v in items:
1109 if isinstance(v, (bool, str, bytes)):
1110 raise ValueError(err_msg)
1111 try:
1112 vals.append(operator.index(v))
1113 except TypeError:
1114 raise ValueError(err_msg) from None
1115 if not vals:
1116 return None
1117 if len(vals) == 1 and vals[0] < 0:
1118 return None
1119 if any(v < 0 for v in vals):
1120 raise ValueError(f"invalid start={start!r}: column indices must be non-negative")
1121 return sorted(set(vals))
1122
1123
1124def _start_key_suffix(start_list: Optional[List[int]]) -> str:
1125 """Returns the cache key suffix ':start=a,b,c' for a normalized start list ('' if unset)."""
1126 if not start_list:
1127 return ""
1128 return ":start=" + ",".join(str(c) for c in start_list)
1129
1130
1131def _format_start_list(start_list: List[int], max_show: int = 8) -> str:
1132 """Formats a start list for messages, showing at most `max_show` entries (as the dist_m4ri binary)."""
1133 shown = ",".join(str(c) for c in start_list[:max_show])
1134 return shown + (",..." if len(start_list) > max_show else "")
1135
1136
1137def _warn_disabled_options(noscan: Any = 0, cbeg: Any = None, cend: Any = None) -> None:
1138 """
1139 Issues a warning to stderr for each of the expert options noscan, cbeg, and cend that is set.
1140 These options are disabled in the Python interface: they are accepted for backward compatibility
1141 but ignored, since their results are not valid distance bounds on their own.
1142 """
1143 for name, val, is_flag in (("noscan", noscan, True), ("cbeg", cbeg, False), ("cend", cend, False)):
1144 if val is None:
1145 continue
1146 try:
1147 ival = int(val)
1148 active = (ival != 0) if is_flag else (ival >= 0)
1149 except (TypeError, ValueError):
1150 active = True
1151 if active:
1152 sys.stderr.write(
1153 f"# Warning: {name}={val} is disabled in the Python interface (ignored); "
1154 f"use the dist_m4ri binary directly\n"
1155 )
1156
1157
1158def _start_warning_text(start_list: List[int]) -> str:
1159 """Returns the stderr warning for a CC start list (same wording as the dist_m4ri binary)."""
1160 return (
1161 f"# WARNING: start={_format_start_list(start_list)} (expert option): CC clusters are grown only from "
1162 f"{len(start_list)} listed column(s)\n"
1163 f"# (not limited to larger column indices); dmin is valid only if a code symmetry maps every\n"
1164 f"# minimum-weight codeword to one containing a listed column\n"
1165 )
1166
1167
1168def _ksub_warning_text(ksub: int) -> str:
1169 """Returns the stderr warning for the experimental RW option ksub (same wording as the dist_m4ri binary)."""
1170 return (
1171 f"# WARNING: ksub={ksub} is experimental and should not be used: a RW step reduces the span of ksub rows\n"
1172 f"# of a fixed basis of ker(H), so that a few codewords are found much more often than others; with\n"
1173 f"# min_hits, RW may end early, and exp(-<n>) underestimates the probability to miss a lighter codeword\n"
1174 )
1175
1176
1177def _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub: Any, method: int, solver: str = "dist_m4ri") -> None:
1178 """
1179 Issues the warning for the experimental RW option ksub > 0 to stderr (with or without min_hits), if RW runs
1180 (method=1 or 3) with the dist_m4ri binary.
1181 """
1182 try:
1183 ival = int(ksub or 0)
1184 except (TypeError, ValueError):
1185 return
1186 if ival > 0 and (int(method) & 1) and solver != "codedistance":
1187 sys.stderr.write(_ksub_warning_text(ival))
1188
1189
1190def _check_kwargs(func: Callable[..., Any], kwargs: Dict[str, Any], aliases: Sequence[str] = ("win",)) -> None:
1191 """
1192 Raises TypeError for the keyword arguments in kwargs (the **kwargs of func) other than the accepted aliases
1193 (`win` for kwin), e.g., misspelled or unsupported options, with the closest parameter names as hints.
1194 """
1195 unknown = [k for k in kwargs if k not in aliases]
1196 if not unknown:
1197 return
1198 import difflib
1199 import inspect
1200 names = [n for n, p in inspect.signature(func).parameters.items() if p.kind is not inspect.Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD]
1201 names += list(aliases)
1202 items = []
1203 for k in unknown:
1204 close = difflib.get_close_matches(k, names, n=1)
1205 items.append(f"'{k}'" + (f" (did you mean '{close[0]}'?)" if close else ""))
1206 if len(items) == 1:
1207 raise TypeError(f"{func.__name__}() got an unexpected keyword argument {items[0]}")
1208 raise TypeError(f"{func.__name__}() got unexpected keyword arguments {', '.join(items)}")
1209
1210
1211def _prepare_start_option(
1212 start: Any,
1213 trust_start: bool = False,
1214 noscan: Any = 0,
1215 cbeg: Any = None,
1216 cend: Any = None,
1217 solver: str = "dist_m4ri"
1218) -> Optional[List[int]]:
1219 """
1220 Validates the expert CC options of a compute_*_distance() call and issues the warnings to stderr.
1221
1222 Returns:
1223 The normalized start list, or None if unset (or not applicable to the selected solver).
1224 """
1225 _warn_disabled_options(noscan, cbeg, cend)
1226 start_list = _normalize_start_list(start)
1227 if start_list is None:
1228 if trust_start:
1229 sys.stderr.write("# Warning: trust_start=1 has no effect without a start list\n")
1230 return None
1231 if solver == "codedistance":
1232 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: start={_format_start_list(start_list)} is ignored with solver='codedistance'\n")
1233 return None
1234 msg = _start_warning_text(start_list)
1235 if _use_distance_cache and trust_start:
1236 msg += "# trust_start=1: start-list results are accepted as valid and copied to the main cache record\n"
1237 elif _use_distance_cache:
1238 msg += (
1239 "# results are cached under a separate ':start=...' key; only dmax and codewords update the\n"
1240 "# main cache record (use trust_start=1 to also accept dmin)\n"
1241 )
1242 sys.stderr.write(msg)
1243 return start_list
1244
1245
1246def _seed_bounds_from_entry(eff_dmin: int, eff_dmax: int, entry: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Tuple[int, int]:
1247 """
1248 Tightens the bounds (eff_dmin, eff_dmax) with those stored in a cache entry (a CSS code is cached as the
1249 records of its two sectors, see _matrix_cache_key()).
1250 """
1251 if not entry:
1252 return eff_dmin, eff_dmax
1253 c_dmin = entry.get("dmin", 0) or 0
1254 c_dmax = entry.get("dmax", 0) or 0
1255 if c_dmax > 0:
1256 eff_dmax = min(eff_dmax, c_dmax) if eff_dmax > 0 else c_dmax
1257 if c_dmin > 1:
1258 eff_dmin = max(eff_dmin, c_dmin) if eff_dmin > 1 else c_dmin
1259 return eff_dmin, eff_dmax
1260
1261
1262def _union_cws(base: Optional[List[List[int]]], extra: Optional[List[List[int]]]) -> List[List[int]]:
1263 """Returns the union of two codeword lists (duplicates removed, sorted by weight)."""
1264 combined = [list(cw) for cw in (base or [])]
1265 seen = {tuple(cw) for cw in combined}
1266 for cw in (extra or []):
1267 t = tuple(cw)
1268 if t not in seen:
1269 combined.append(list(cw))
1270 seen.add(t)
1271 combined.sort(key=len)
1272 return combined
1273
1274
1275def _dist_from_bounds(dmin: int, dmax: int) -> int:
1276 """The distance reported for the bounds [dmin, dmax]: dmin if exact or without an upper bound, otherwise dmax."""
1277 return dmin if (dmin == dmax or dmax == 0) else dmax
1278
1279
1280def _single_entry_is_exact(entry: Dict[str, Any], need_cws: bool = False, dstop: int = 0) -> bool:
1281 """
1282 Cache hit test for a classical / quantum / DEM entry: the exact distance, or with the stop target dstop > 0 a
1283 lower bound dmin >= dstop (and codewords if needed).
1284 """
1285 c_dmin = entry.get("dmin", 0) or 0
1286 if not ((c_dmin > 0 and c_dmin == entry.get("dmax")) or (dstop > 0 and c_dmin >= dstop)):
1287 return False
1288 return (not need_cws) or bool(entry.get("cws"))
1289
1290
1291def _merge_start_into_plain(
1292 plain_key: str,
1293 src: Dict[str, Any],
1294 trust: bool = False,
1295 rw_delta: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None
1296) -> bool:
1297 """
1298 Merges the start-list cache record `src` (key plain_key + ':start=...') into the main record `plain_key`.
1299
1300 The upper bound dmax (minimum of the positive values) and the codewords (union) are always valid and
1301 are always merged. Only with `trust` (expert option trust_start) the lower bound dmin is merged as well
1302 (maximum, capped at dmax), and rw_steps are either incremented by the steps of the run, `rw_delta`
1303 (after a calculation), or set to the maximum of the two records (copy of a cached record, rw_delta=None).
1304 (A CSS code is cached as the records of its two sectors, see _matrix_cache_key().)
1305
1306 Args:
1307 plain_key: Main cache key.
1308 src: Start-list cache record.
1309 trust: Accept the start-list lower bound as valid.
1310 rw_delta: RW steps of the run, {'': steps}.
1311
1312 Returns:
1313 True if the main record was created or modified.
1314 """
1315 global _distance_cache
1316 prev = _distance_cache.get(plain_key)
1317 new: Dict[str, Any] = dict(prev) if prev else {}
1318 s_dmin = src.get("dmin", 0) or 0
1319 s_dmax = src.get("dmax", 0) or 0
1320 p_dmin = new.get("dmin", 0) or 0
1321 p_dmax = new.get("dmax", 0) or 0
1322 p_rw = new.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0
1323 dmax = min(p_dmax, s_dmax) if (p_dmax > 0 and s_dmax > 0) else (p_dmax if p_dmax > 0 else s_dmax)
1324 dmin, rw = p_dmin, p_rw
1325 if trust:
1326 dmin = max(p_dmin, s_dmin)
1327 if rw_delta is not None:
1328 rw = p_rw + (rw_delta.get("", 0) or 0)
1329 else:
1330 rw = max(p_rw, src.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0)
1331 if dmax > 0 and dmin > dmax:
1332 dmin = dmax
1333 s_cws = src.get("cws", []) or []
1334 if not prev and not (trust or s_dmax > 0 or s_cws):
1335 return False
1336 new["cws"] = _union_cws(new.get("cws", []), s_cws)
1337 new["dist"] = _dist_from_bounds(dmin, dmax)
1338 new["dmin"], new["dmax"], new["rw_steps"] = dmin, dmax, rw
1339 new["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(dmin, dmax, rw)
1340 _distance_cache[plain_key] = new
1341 return True
1342
1343
1344def _resolve_start_cache(
1345 plain_key: str,
1346 start_list: Optional[List[int]],
1347 is_hit: Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], bool],
1348 trust_start: bool,
1349 merge_copy: Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], bool],
1350 eff_cache_file: Optional[str],
1351 verbose: bool = False
1352) -> Tuple[str, Optional[Dict[str, Any]], Optional[Dict[str, Any]]]:
1353 """
1354 Resolves the cache record of a run with an optional expert CC start list.
1355
1356 Without a start list, or if the main record already holds the requested exact result, the main record
1357 is used. Otherwise the separate start-list record (key plain_key + ':start=a,b,c') is used; with
1358 trust_start, an existing exact start-list record is copied to the main record (via `merge_copy`), and
1359 the cache file is saved, even though no calculation is needed.
1360
1361 Returns:
1362 (code_key, cached_entry, plain_entry): the key and the existing record (or None) for the results of
1363 this run, and the main record (or None) used to seed the bounds of a start-list run.
1364 """
1365 plain_entry = _distance_cache.get(plain_key)
1366 if not start_list:
1367 return plain_key, plain_entry, None
1368 if plain_entry is not None and is_hit(plain_entry):
1369 if verbose:
1370 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Start list not needed: the main record '{plain_key}' has the exact distance")
1371 return plain_key, plain_entry, None
1372 code_key = plain_key + _start_key_suffix(start_list)
1373 cached_entry = _distance_cache.get(code_key)
1374 if trust_start and cached_entry is not None and is_hit(cached_entry):
1375 if merge_copy(cached_entry) and eff_cache_file:
1376 save_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
1377 if verbose:
1378 print(f"[dist_m4ri] trust_start: copied the exact start-list record to the main record '{plain_key}'")
1379 return code_key, cached_entry, plain_entry
1380
1381
1382def run_dist_m4ri(
1383 dist_m4ri_path: Optional[str] = None,
1384 method: int = 3,
1385 finH: Optional[str] = None,
1386 finG: Optional[str] = None,
1387 finL: Optional[str] = None,
1388 fin: Optional[str] = None,
1389 finC: Optional[str] = None,
1390 fdem: Optional[str] = None,
1391 dmin: int = 0,
1392 dmax: int = 0,
1393 wmax: int = 0,
1394 wmin: int = 1,
1395 dexp: int = 0,
1396 dest: int = 0,
1397 dstop: int = 0,
1398 steps: Optional[int] = None,
1399 threads: Optional[int] = None,
1400 timeout: float = 60.0,
1401 smax: Optional[int] = None,
1402 start: Optional[Union[int, str, Sequence[int]]] = None,
1403 cbeg: Optional[int] = None,
1404 cend: Optional[int] = None,
1405 css: Optional[int] = None,
1406 noscan: int = 0,
1407 classical: int = -1,
1408 dW: int = -1,
1409 maxC: int = 0,
1410 pmin: float = 0.0,
1411 merge: bool = True,
1412 drop: Optional[str] = None,
1413 outD: Optional[str] = None,
1414 sort_rows: Optional[bool] = None,
1415 outC: Optional[str] = None,
1416 seed: int = 0,
1417 debug: int = 0,
1418 nothrottle: bool = False,
1419 chunk_size: int = 0,
1420 ksub: int = 0,
1421 kwin: int = 0,
1422 win_mode: int = 0,
1423 win_hyb: int = 0,
1424 pairs: int = -1,
1425 min_hits: Optional[int] = None,
1426 cov_cws: int = 100,
1427 refresh: int = 0,
1428 verbose: bool = False,
1429 stop_event: Optional[threading.Event] = None,
1430 warn_start: bool = True,
1431 warn_ksub: bool = True
1432) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
1433 """
1434 Low-level invocation of the multithreaded dist_m4ri binary.
1435
1436 DEM input:
1437 merge: If True (default), the binary merges the equal columns of the DEM fdem (error mechanisms with the
1438 same detectors and observables). Exact: dropping two equal columns of a codeword gives a lighter one,
1439 so the distance does not change. Column indices (finC, outC, start) are those of the DEM; the codewords
1440 found use the first one of each set of equal columns. merge=False passes merge=0 (all columns are
1441 kept, e.g., to enumerate the codewords with each of them). Ignored without fdem.
1442 drop: The detectors of the DEM fdem to drop if this is verified to be exact, passed as drop=...: None (the
1443 binary's default, drop=auto: a search for the largest such set in the DEM), "auto" or "1" (the same), "0"
1444 (keep all detectors), or a file with the detectors to drop (0-based; otherwise, the binary uses the full DEM
1445 and prints a note, see _parse_stderr_stats()). Ignored without fdem.
1446 outD: File to which the binary writes the detectors dropped from the DEM fdem (0-based; only the comment line
1447 '# N of M detectors dropped ...' if none, see read_drop_file()). Ignored without fdem.
1448
1449 Row order:
1450 sort_rows: Passed as sort_rows=1 (True) or sort_rows=0 (False); None (default): the binary's default, i.e.,
1451 1 for matrices and 0 for a DEM. With sort_rows=1, the binary sorts the rows of H by increasing weight
1452 (stable), which reduces the CC work for matrices with very different row weights (e.g., 1.7-4x with the
1453 hook columns of an extended CSS distance); the detectors of a DEM are in time order, which is better for
1454 CC (use sort_rows=False also for matrices exported from a DEM). The distance and RW do not depend on the
1455 order of the rows; CC enumerates the same codewords, possibly in another order and with other hit counts.
1456
1457 RW windows:
1458 kwin / win_mode: A window of kwin columns in every RW step (win_mode=0: a Tanner graph ball, 1: an index
1459 window). kwin=0 (default): the automatic hybrid for n >= 500, an index window of win_hyb columns in every
1460 other step and uniform random permutations in the others.
1461 win_hyb: Window size of the hybrid RW steps, passed as win_hyb=N if nonzero; 0 (default): 256 columns for a
1462 DEM, 512 for matrices (at most 3n/4). The windows of 192-256 columns find the minimum-weight codewords of
1463 circuit DEMs 2-10 times faster than 512, and windows of one round of columns are much slower. With
1464 debug & 1 (or verbose=True), the binary prints the rounds of a DEM (estimated from the time translation of
1465 its errors: D detectors and L columns per round, also in _last_run_stats["rounds"]) and the codewords found
1466 by the uniform and by the window steps (see _parse_stderr_stats()).
1467
1468 RW pairs:
1469 pairs: The RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, as in Lee-Brickell and Stern), passed as pairs=N if not -1: a
1470 RW step also finds the codewords with two non-pivot columns, checking only the pairs which agree on N
1471 random pivot rows (0: off). -1 (default): auto, about one non-pivot column per bucket, with fewer rows
1472 while a codeword of the weight of the upper bound would be kept with probability below 0.8. The pairs
1473 find the minimum-weight codewords of circuit DEMs 7-25 times faster (per wall time) and lighter
1474 codewords of codes with a large distance. With debug & 1, the binary prints the pairs checked per step
1475 and the codewords found by pairs and by single columns (also in _last_run_stats).
1476
1477 Stop target:
1478 dstop: The run (method=2 or 3) ends once CC has certified dmin >= dstop, i.e., that there is no codeword of
1479 weight < dstop, unless a lighter codeword is found (default: 0 = off). Unlike dmax, dstop is not an
1480 upper bound and is not reported as dmax: the result is (dmin, w, rw_steps), where w is the weight of the
1481 lightest codeword found (0: none).
1482
1483 Expert CC options:
1484 start: List of CC start columns (int, comma-separated string "a,b,c", or sequence of ints;
1485 None or a single negative value: all columns), passed as start=a,b,c (sorted, distinct).
1486 CC clusters are grown only from the listed columns, and they are not limited to larger
1487 column indices. WARNING: the returned dmin (and an exact result) is valid only if a code
1488 symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword to one containing a listed column (e.g., one
1489 column per block of a quasi-cyclic code); dmax is always valid.
1490 warn_start: If True (default), issue the start-list warning to stderr.
1491 noscan / cbeg / cend: Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility,
1492 but ignored with a warning to stderr (use the dist_m4ri binary directly).
1493
1494 Experimental RW option:
1495 ksub: Experimental, should not be used: subspace dimension sampled from ker(H) in RW (0: full-matrix RW).
1496 A RW step reduces the span of ksub rows of a fixed basis of ker(H), so that a few codewords are found
1497 much more often than others (min_hits may end RW early).
1498 warn_ksub: If True (default), issue the warning for ksub > 0 to stderr (with method=1 or 3).
1499
1500 Debug output:
1501 debug: Debug bitmap; the bits in BIN_DBG_MASK are passed to the binary (its diagnostic output on stderr
1502 is printed), and PY_DBG_COMMANDS echoes the command line and the run time. verbose=True implies
1503 the bits VERBOSE_DEBUG.
1504
1505 Cancellation:
1506 stop_event: Optional threading.Event; once it is set, the binary is terminated and RuntimeError is raised
1507 (the binary is also terminated on any other exception, e.g., KeyboardInterrupt).
1508
1509 Returns:
1510 tuple (dmin, dmax, rw_steps)
1511 """
1512 global _last_run_stats
1513 exec_path = find_dist_m4ri_binary(dist_m4ri_path)
1514
1515 start_list = _normalize_start_list(start)
1516 _warn_disabled_options(noscan, cbeg, cend)
1517 if start_list and warn_start:
1518 sys.stderr.write(_start_warning_text(start_list))
1519 if warn_ksub:
1520 _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub, method)
1521
1522 finC = check_finc_outc(finC, outC, verbose=False)
1523
1524 if method == 2 and wmax <= 0:
1525 if dmax > 0:
1526 wmax = dmax
1527 elif timeout <= 0.0 and dstop <= 0:
1528 raise ValueError(
1529 "either parameter wmax>0, dmax>0, dstop>0, or timeout>0 should be specified for CC method=2."
1530 )
1531
1532 eff_debug = (debug | VERBOSE_DEBUG) if verbose else debug
1533 bin_debug = eff_debug & BIN_DBG_MASK # the higher bits are used by the Python wrapper only
1534 cmd = [exec_path, f"debug={bin_debug}", f"method={method}"]
1535
1536 if finH: cmd.append(f"finH={finH}")
1537 if finG: cmd.append(f"finG={finG}")
1538 if finL: cmd.append(f"finL={finL}")
1539 if fin: cmd.append(f"fin={fin}")
1540 if finC: cmd.append(f"finC={finC}")
1541 if fdem: cmd.append(f"fdem={fdem}")
1542 if dmin > 0: cmd.append(f"dmin={dmin}")
1543 if dmax > 0: cmd.append(f"dmax={dmax}")
1544 if dstop > 0: cmd.append(f"dstop={dstop}")
1545 if wmax > 0: cmd.append(f"wmax={wmax}")
1546 if wmin is not None and wmin != 1: cmd.append(f"wmin={wmin}")
1547 if dexp > 0: cmd.append(f"dexp={dexp}")
1548 elif dest > 0: cmd.append(f"dest={dest}")
1549 if steps is not None and steps >= 0: cmd.append(f"steps={steps}")
1550 if threads is not None and threads > 0: cmd.append(f"threads={threads}")
1551 if timeout is not None and timeout >= 0: cmd.append(f"timeout={timeout}")
1552 if smax is not None: cmd.append(f"smax={smax}")
1553 if start_list: cmd.append("start=" + ",".join(str(c) for c in start_list))
1554 if css is not None: cmd.append(f"css={css}")
1555 if classical >= 0: cmd.append(f"classical={classical}")
1556 if dW >= 0: cmd.append(f"dW={dW}")
1557 if maxC > 0: cmd.append(f"maxC={maxC}")
1558 if pmin > 0.0: cmd.append(f"pmin={pmin}")
1559 if fdem and not merge: cmd.append("merge=0")
1560 if fdem and drop: cmd.append(f"drop={drop}")
1561 if fdem and outD: cmd.append(f"outD={outD}")
1562 if sort_rows is not None: cmd.append(f"sort_rows={1 if sort_rows else 0}")
1563 if outC: cmd.append(f"outC={outC}")
1564 if seed != 0: cmd.append(f"seed={seed}")
1565 if nothrottle: cmd.append("nothrottle=1")
1566 if chunk_size > 0: cmd.append(f"chunk_size={chunk_size}")
1567 if ksub > 0: cmd.append(f"ksub={ksub}")
1568 if kwin > 0: cmd.append(f"kwin={kwin}")
1569 if win_mode != 0: cmd.append(f"win_mode={win_mode}")
1570 if win_hyb != 0: cmd.append(f"win_hyb={win_hyb}")
1571 if pairs != -1: cmd.append(f"pairs={pairs}")
1572 if min_hits is not None and min_hits >= 0: cmd.append(f"min_hits={min_hits}")
1573 if cov_cws != 100: cmd.append(f"cov_cws={cov_cws}")
1574 if refresh > 0: cmd.append(f"refresh={refresh}")
1575
1576 if eff_debug & PY_DBG_COMMANDS:
1577 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Running: {' '.join(cmd)}")
1578
1579 t_start = time.time()
1580 proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
1581 try:
1582 if stop_event is None:
1583 stdout, stderr = proc.communicate()
1584 else:
1585 while True: # communicate() with a timeout keeps draining the pipes (no deadlock on a full pipe)
1586 try:
1587 stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(timeout=0.05)
1588 break
1589 except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
1590 if stop_event.is_set():
1591 raise RuntimeError("dist_m4ri execution cancelled by stop_event")
1592 except BaseException: # cancelled, KeyboardInterrupt, ...: do not leave the child process running
1593 try:
1594 proc.terminate()
1595 proc.communicate(timeout=1.0)
1596 except Exception:
1597 try:
1598 proc.kill()
1599 proc.wait()
1600 except Exception:
1601 pass
1602 raise
1603
1604 if eff_debug & PY_DBG_COMMANDS:
1605 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Finished in {time.time() - t_start:.3f} s (exit code {proc.returncode})")
1606
1607 if proc.returncode != 0:
1608 raise RuntimeError(f"dist_m4ri failed with exit code {proc.returncode}:\n{stderr}")
1609
1610 _last_run_stats = _parse_stderr_stats(stderr)
1611 if (verbose or bin_debug > 0) and stderr:
1612 print(stderr.rstrip())
1613
1614 return parse_dist_m4ri_output(stdout)
1615

1617def _matrix_to_file(matrix, extension: str = ".mtx", temp_dir: str = "tmp") -> str:
1618 """Helper to convert a matrix (numpy or scipy sparse) or file path to an MTX file path."""
1619 if isinstance(matrix, (str, Path)):
1620 return str(matrix)
1621
1622 import numpy as np
1623 from scipy.io import mmwrite
1624 from scipy.sparse import csr_matrix, issparse
1625
1626 path = create_unique_file(directory=temp_dir, extension=extension)
1627 if issparse(matrix):
1628 csr = matrix.astype(np.int8)
1629 mmwrite(path, csr, symmetry='general')
1630 else:
1631 mat_arr = np.asarray(matrix, dtype=np.int8)
1632 csr = csr_matrix(mat_arr)
1633 mmwrite(path, csr, symmetry='general')
1634 return path

1637def has_noise(circuit: Any) -> bool:
1638 """
1639 Checks if a Stim circuit has noise: a noise channel (e.g., DEPOLARIZE1, X_ERROR, PAULI_CHANNEL_2, E, or
1640 HERALDED_ERASE), or a measurement with a flip probability (e.g., M(0.001) or MPP(0.01)), i.e., if strip_noise()
1641 changes it.
1642 """
1643 try:
1644 stim = _get_stim()
1645 except ImportError:
1646 return False
1647 if not isinstance(circuit, stim.Circuit):
1648 return False
1649 return circuit.without_noise() != circuit
1650
1651
1652def strip_noise(circuit: Any) -> Any:
1653 """
1654 Removes all noise from a Stim circuit (stim.Circuit or a .stim file), see stim.Circuit.without_noise(): the noise
1655 channels (e.g., DEPOLARIZE1, X_ERROR, PAULI_CHANNEL_2, E) are removed, the measurements lose their flip
1656 probabilities (M(0.001) becomes M), and heralded noise (e.g., HERALDED_ERASE) is replaced by MPAD, so that the
1657 measurement record does not change. E.g., add_noise(strip_noise(circuit), p) (or add_noise(circuit, p,
1658 force=True); CLI: --force-noise) gives circuits with the same noise model.
1659
1660 Returns:
1661 The noiseless stim.Circuit.
1662 """
1663 stim = _get_stim()
1664 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
1665 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
1666 return circuit.without_noise()
1667
1668
1669def _add_noise_recursive(
1670 circuit: Any, p: float, num_qubits: int, active_qubits: Set[int]
1671) -> Any:
1672 """Recursively adds uniform circuit-level noise to a Stim circuit (see add_noise())."""
1673 stim = _get_stim()
1674 p1 = 0.1 * p # one-qubit depolarizing noise (after one-qubit gates, on idle qubits)
1675 noisy_circuit = stim.Circuit()
1676 for inst in circuit:
1677 if isinstance(inst, stim.CircuitRepeatBlock):
1678 noisy_body = _add_noise_recursive(
1679 inst.body_copy(), p, num_qubits, active_qubits
1680 )
1681 noisy_circuit.append(
1682 stim.CircuitRepeatBlock(inst.repeat_count, noisy_body)
1683 )
1684 continue
1685 name = inst.name
1686 if name == "TICK":
1687 idle_qubits = set(range(num_qubits)) - active_qubits
1688 if idle_qubits:
1689 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", sorted(idle_qubits), p1)
1690 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
1691 active_qubits.clear()
1692 continue
1693 gd = stim.gate_data(name)
1694 noise_channel = gd.is_noisy_gate and (not gd.produces_measurements or 0 not in gd.num_parens_arguments_range)
1695 if name == "MPAD" or noise_channel or not (gd.is_unitary or gd.is_reset or gd.produces_measurements):
1696 # annotations (DETECTOR, OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE, QUBIT_COORDS, SHIFT_COORDS), MPAD (its targets are bits, not
1697 # qubits), and the noise channels of a noisy circuit (also HERALDED_ERASE): no noise, not an operation
1698 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
1699 continue
1700 targets = inst.targets_copy()
1701 # qubit_value is None for measurement records (rec[-k]), sweep bits (sweep[k]), and combiners (*)
1702 qubits = [t.qubit_value for t in targets if t.qubit_value is not None]
1703 active_qubits.update(qubits)
1704 flip = "Z_ERROR" if name.endswith("X") else "X_ERROR" # (RX, MX, MRX: X basis; Z or Y basis otherwise)
1705 if gd.produces_measurements and gd.is_single_qubit_gate: # M, MX, MY, MR, MRX, MRY
1706 if qubits:
1707 noisy_circuit.append(flip, qubits, p)
1708 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
1709 if gd.is_reset and qubits:
1710 noisy_circuit.append(flip, qubits, p)
1711 elif gd.is_reset and not gd.produces_measurements: # R, RX, RY
1712 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
1713 if qubits:
1714 noisy_circuit.append(flip, qubits, p)
1715 elif gd.is_unitary and gd.is_single_qubit_gate: # I, X, H, H_XY, S, SQRT_X, C_XYZ, ...
1716 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
1717 if qubits:
1718 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", qubits, p1)
1719 elif gd.is_unitary and gd.is_two_qubit_gate: # CX, CZ, XCY, SWAP, ISWAP, SQRT_XX, CXSWAP, II, ...
1720 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
1721 pair_qubits: List[int] = []
1722 ctrl_qubits: List[int] = [] # the qubits of the classically controlled pairs (e.g., CX rec[-1] 5)
1723 for a, b in zip(targets[::2], targets[1::2]):
1724 if a.qubit_value is not None and b.qubit_value is not None:
1725 pair_qubits += [a.qubit_value, b.qubit_value]
1726 else:
1727 ctrl_qubits += [t.qubit_value for t in (a, b) if t.qubit_value is not None]
1728 if pair_qubits:
1729 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE2", pair_qubits, p)
1730 if ctrl_qubits:
1731 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", ctrl_qubits, p1)
1732 else: # multi-qubit measurements (MPP, MXX, MYY, MZZ) and Pauli product gates (SPP, SPP_DAG): no noise
1733 noisy_circuit.append(inst)
1734 return noisy_circuit
1735
1736
1737def add_noise(circuit: Any, p: float = 0.001, force: bool = False) -> Any:
1738 """
1739 Adds uniform circuit-level noise of strength p to a Stim circuit (the gates are classified by stim.gate_data()):
1740 - DEPOLARIZE2(p) after two-qubit gates (CX, CY, CZ, XCX, XCY, XCZ, YCX, YCY, YCZ, SWAP, ISWAP, ISWAP_DAG, SQRT_XX,
1741 SQRT_YY, SQRT_ZZ and their _DAG versions, CXSWAP, SWAPCX, CZSWAP, II); a classically controlled gate (e.g.,
1742 CX rec[-1] 5 or CZ sweep[0] 5) gets DEPOLARIZE1(p/10) on its qubit;
1743 - DEPOLARIZE1(p/10) after one-qubit gates (I, X, Y, Z, H, H_XY, H_YZ, S, S_DAG, SQRT_X, SQRT_Y and their _DAG
1744 versions, C_XYZ, C_ZYX, and the other variants), and on the qubits idle since the previous TICK (at each TICK,
1745 and at the end of the circuit);
1746 - X (Z) flips with probability p after Z-basis or Y-basis (X-basis) resets and before measurements, both before and
1747 after a measurement with reset (MR, MRX, MRY);
1748 - none for the multi-qubit measurements (MPP, MXX, MYY, MZZ) and the Pauli product gates (SPP, SPP_DAG).
1749 The noise of a noisy circuit is kept, unless force=True: then it is replaced (see strip_noise()).
1750
1751 Args:
1752 circuit: stim.Circuit or path to a .stim file.
1753 p: Noise strength (for the distance, only which errors are possible matters); p=0: no noise is added.
1754 force: If True, all noise of the circuit is removed first (with p=0: only that).
1755
1756 Returns:
1757 The noisy stim.Circuit (a copy).
1758 """
1759 stim = _get_stim()
1760 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
1761 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
1762 if force:
1763 circuit = strip_noise(circuit)
1764 if p <= 0.0:
1765 return circuit.copy()
1766 num_qubits = circuit.num_qubits
1767 active_qubits: Set[int] = set()
1768 noisy_circuit = _add_noise_recursive(circuit, p, num_qubits, active_qubits)
1769 if active_qubits:
1770 final_idle_qubits = set(range(num_qubits)) - active_qubits
1771 if final_idle_qubits:
1772 noisy_circuit.append("DEPOLARIZE1", sorted(final_idle_qubits), 0.1 * p)
1773 return noisy_circuit
1774
1775
1776def remove_empty_detectors(circuit: Any) -> Tuple[Any, int]:
1777 """Removes DETECTOR instructions that have no measurement record targets."""
1778 stim = _get_stim()
1779 new_circuit = stim.Circuit()
1780 removed = 0
1781 for inst in circuit:
1782 if isinstance(inst, stim.CircuitRepeatBlock):
1783 body, r = remove_empty_detectors(inst.body_copy())
1784 removed += r * inst.repeat_count
1785 new_circuit.append(stim.CircuitRepeatBlock(inst.repeat_count, body))
1786 elif inst.name == "DETECTOR":
1787 rec_targets = [
1788 t for t in inst.targets_copy()
1789 if t.is_measurement_record_target
1790 ]
1791 if not rec_targets:
1792 removed += 1
1793 else:
1794 new_circuit.append(inst)
1795 else:
1796 new_circuit.append(inst)
1797 return new_circuit, removed
1798
1799
1800def has_repeat_block(circuit: Any) -> bool:
1801 """Checks if a Stim circuit contains at least one REPEAT block."""
1802 stim = _get_stim()
1803 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
1804 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
1805 if not isinstance(circuit, stim.Circuit):
1806 return False
1807 for inst in circuit:
1808 if isinstance(inst, stim.CircuitRepeatBlock):
1809 return True
1810 return False
