3913) -> Any:
3914 """
3915 Computes the minimum distance of a single-sided quantum code given parity check matrix H
3916 and degeneracy generator G (or logical operator matrix L).
3917
3918 Args:
3919 H: Parity check matrix (numpy array, scipy sparse matrix, or file path).
3920 G: Degeneracy generator matrix (numpy array, scipy sparse matrix, or file path).
3921 L: Logical operator matrix (numpy array, scipy sparse matrix, or file path).
3922 dist_m4ri: Path to dist_m4ri executable (optional).
3923 method: Solver method (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing default).
3924 threads: Maximum number of worker threads (default: all logical CPUs available; subject to throttling).
3925 timeout: Execution timeout in seconds.
3926 num_steps: Maximum RW steps.
3927 d_exp: Expected distance estimate.
3928 d_min / dmin: Known lower bound on distance.
3929 d_max / dmax: Known upper bound on distance.
3930 dstop: Stop target for the lower bound (default: 0 = off): the search ends once CC has certified
3931 dmin >= dstop (method=2 or 3), unless a lighter codeword is found. Unlike dmax, dstop is not an upper
3932 bound, and it is not reported as dmax: d_info = [dmin, w, rw_steps] with dmin >= dstop and the weight w
3933 of the lightest codeword found (0: none). A cached lower bound dmin >= dstop answers the request without
3934 a calculation.
3935 wmin: Minimum distance of interest (terminate early if cw of weight <= wmin is found in RW or CC, default: 1).
3936 wmax: Maximum weight to search in CC.
3937 smax: Maximum syndrome weight for CC confinement profile.
3938 start: Expert option: list of CC start columns (int, comma-separated string "a,b,c", or
3939 sequence of ints; None or -1: all columns). CC clusters are grown only from the listed
3940 columns, and they are not limited to larger column indices. WARNING: the lower bound
3941 (and an exact result) is valid only if a code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword
3942 to one containing a listed column (e.g., one column per block of a quasi-cyclic code);
3943 the upper bound is always valid. Results are cached under the separate key
3944 '<key>:start=a,b,c'; only dmax and codewords update the main cache record.
3945 trust_start: Expert option: accept the start-list results as valid, i.e., also merge dmin and
3946 rw_steps into the main cache record, and copy an existing exact start-list record to the
3947 main record even if no calculation is needed (default: False).
3948 cbeg / cend / noscan: Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility,
3949 but ignored with a warning to stderr (use the dist_m4ri binary directly).
3950 sort_rows: Row order of H in the binary (see run_dist_m4ri()): True sorts the rows by increasing weight
3951 (faster CC for very different row weights), False keeps their order, and None (default) leaves the
3952 binary's default (sorted for matrices; the detectors of a DEM are kept in time order). The result and
3953 the cache key do not depend on it.
3954 win_hyb: Window size of the automatic hybrid RW steps (kwin=0, n >= 500: a window on every other step; see
3955 run_dist_m4ri()); 0 (default): 256 columns for a DEM, 512 for matrices. The cache key does not depend on
3956 it.
3957 pairs: The RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, see run_dist_m4ri()): the number of random pivot rows of
3958 their buckets (0: off; -1, the default: auto). The cache key does not depend on it.
3959 ksub: Experimental, should not be used (a warning is printed to stderr for ksub > 0 with method=1 or 3):
3960 subspace dimension sampled from ker(H) in RW (default: 0, full-matrix RW).
3961 dW: Extra weight window above dmin to collect codewords.
3962 maxC: Maximum number of codewords to collect.
3963 finC: Input file with initial codewords.
3964 outC: Output file to save codewords (NZLIST format).
3965 do_cws: Whether to return extracted codewords.
3966 return_info: If True, return (dist, d_info) or (dist, d_info, cws) where d_info is [dmin, dmax, num_rw].
3967 cache_file: Optional JSON file path for persistent distance caching.
3968 solver: "dist_m4ri" or "codedistance".
3969 codedistance_method: Method if using codedistance library.
3970 codedistance_params: Extra parameters for codedistance library.
3971 seed: Random seed.
3972 debug: Debug bitmap: the bits in BIN_DBG_MASK for the dist_m4ri binary, and the PY_DBG_* bits.
3973 verbose: Verbose reporting flag.
3974
3975 Returns:
3976 dist or (dist, cws) if do_cws is True (or (dist, d_info) / (dist, d_info, cws) if return_info=True)
3977
3978 Raises:

3981 eff_dmin = dmin if dmin > 0 else d_min
3982 eff_dmax = dmax if dmax > 0 else d_max
3983 _check_kwargs(compute_quantum_distance, kwargs)
3984 start_list = _prepare_start_option(start, trust_start, noscan, cbeg, cend, solver)
3985 _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub, method, solver)
3986
3987 if G is None and L is None:
3988 raise ValueError(
3989 "Either G (dual generator matrix) or L (logical operator matrix) "
3990 "must be specified for quantum distance."
3991 )
3992
3993 if solver == "codedistance":
3994 if do_cws or outC:
3995 raise ValueError("Codeword extraction is not supported with codedistance solver; use solver='dist_m4ri'.")
3996 codedistance = _get_codedistance()
3997 import numpy as np
3998 params = dict(codedistance_params or {})
3999 if num_steps is not None and "iterCount" not in params:
4000 params["iterCount"] = num_steps
4001
4002 H_mat = H.toarray() if hasattr(H, 'toarray') else (
4003 np.asarray(H, dtype=np.int8) if isinstance(H, (np.ndarray, list)) else None
4004 )
4005 if G is None and L is not None:
4006 raise ValueError(
4007 "The 'codedistance' solver requires the stabilizer generator matrix G, "
4008 "not the logical operator matrix L. Use solver='dist_m4ri' with L."
4009 )
4010 dual_mat = G if G is not None else L
4011 dual_arr = dual_mat.toarray() if hasattr(dual_mat, 'toarray') else (
4012 np.asarray(dual_mat, dtype=np.int8) if isinstance(dual_mat, (np.ndarray, list)) else None
4013 )
4014
4015 res = codedistance.codeDistance(
4016 H_mat, dual_arr, tB=1, method=codedistance_method, params=params,
4017 seed=seed if seed != 0 else None
4018 )
4019 d = res.get("d", -1)
4020 if return_info:
4021 d_info = format_bounds_list(d, d, 0) if d > 0 else [0, 0, 0]
4022 return d, d_info
4023 return d
4024
4025 # Solver is native multithreaded dist_m4ri (the cache records are shared with the sectors of CSS codes)
4026 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
4027 res = _cached_code_distance(
4028 H, G, L, False, "quantum", dist_m4ri=dist_m4ri, method=method, threads=threads, timeout=timeout,
4029 num_steps=num_steps, d_exp=d_exp, dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=eff_dmax, dstop=dstop, wmin=wmin, wmax=wmax,
4030 smax=smax, start_list=start_list, dW=dW, maxC=maxC, finC=finC, outC=outC, need_cws=bool(do_cws or outC),
4031 eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, seed=seed, debug=debug, verbose=verbose, nothrottle=nothrottle,
4032 chunk_size=chunk_size, ksub=ksub, kwin=kwin if kwin > 0 else int(kwargs.get("win", 0) or 0),
4033 win_mode=win_mode, min_hits=min_hits, cov_cws=cov_cws, refresh=refresh, trust_start=trust_start,
4034 sort_rows=sort_rows, win_hyb=win_hyb, pairs=pairs
4035 )
4036 dist, d_info, cws = res["dist"], res["d_info"], res["cws"]
4037 if return_info:
4038 return (dist, d_info, cws) if do_cws else (dist, d_info)
4039 return (dist, cws) if do_cws else dist

4042def _split_css_filename(filepath: Optional[str], sector: str) -> Optional[str]:
4043 """Generates sector-suffixed filename for CSS codewords (e.g. 'cws.nz' -> 'cws_X.nz')."""
4044 if not filepath:
4045 return None
4046 base, ext = os.path.splitext(filepath)
4047 if not ext:
4048 ext = ".nz"
4049 if base.endswith(f"_{sector}"):
4050 return f"{base}{ext}"
4051 elif base.endswith("_X") or base.endswith("_Z"):
4052 base = base[:-2]
4053 return f"{base}_{sector}{ext}"
4054
4055
4056def _css_sector_finc(finC: Optional[str], outC: Optional[str]) -> Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str]]:
4057 """
4058 Input codeword files (finC_X, finC_Z) of the two CSS sectors: the sector files (e.g. 'cws.nz' -> 'cws_X.nz' and
4059 'cws_Z.nz') which exist and are not empty; if there are none, finC itself for both sectors (codewords which are
4060 not valid in a sector are skipped by the binary), unless finC is identical to outC and does not exist or is
4061 empty (see check_finc_outc()).
4062 """
4063 if not finC:
4064 return None, None
4065 files = [_split_css_filename(finC, s) for s in ("X", "Z")]
4066 files = [f if (os.path.isfile(f) and os.path.getsize(f) > 0) else None for f in files]
4067 if files[0] or files[1]:
4068 return files[0], files[1]
4069 raw = check_finc_outc(finC, outC)
4070 return raw, raw
4071

4085 d_max: int = 0,
4086 dmin: int = 0,
4087 dmax: int = 0,
4088 dstop: int = 0,
4089 wmin: int = 1,
4090 wmax: int = 0,
4091 smax: Optional[int] = None,
4092 start: Optional[Union[int, str, Sequence[int]]] = None,
4093 cbeg: Optional[int] = None,

4102 solver: str = "dist_m4ri",
4103 codedistance_method: str = "QDistEvol",
4104 codedistance_params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
4105 seed: int = 0,
4106 debug: int = 0,
4107 verbose: bool = False,
4108 nothrottle: bool = False,
4109 chunk_size: int = 0,
4110 ksub: int = 0,
4111 kwin: int = 0,
4112 win_mode: int = 0,
4113 win_hyb: int = 0,
4114 pairs: int = -1,
4115 min_hits: Optional[int] = None,
4116 cov_cws: int = 100,
4117 refresh: int = 0,
4118 trust_start: bool = False,
4119 sort_rows: Optional[bool] = None,
4120 **kwargs
4121) -> Tuple[Any, ...]:
4122 """
4123 Computes CSS quantum code distance d = min(d_X, d_Z).
4124
4125 Args:
4126 Hx: X-stabilizer parity check matrix (required, at least one row).
4127 Hz: Z-stabilizer parity check matrix (required, at least one row).
4128 Lx: Optional X-logical operator matrix (alternative to Hz as finG).
4129 Lz: Optional Z-logical operator matrix (alternative to Hx as finG).
4130 dist_m4ri: Path to dist_m4ri executable (optional).
4131 method: Solver method (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing default).
4132 threads: Maximum number of worker threads (default: all logical CPUs available; subject to throttling).
4133 timeout: Execution timeout in seconds.
4134 num_steps: Maximum RW steps.
4135 d_exp: Expected distance estimate.
4136 d_min / dmin: Known lower bound on d = min(dX, dZ), inclusive (a lower bound of both sectors).
4137 d_max / dmax: Known upper bound on d = min(dX, dZ), inclusive. As it is not an upper bound of either
4138 sector, it is passed to both sector runs as the stop target dstop (each sector is needed only up to this
4139 weight), and it is not stored in the sector cache records; the returned d is at most dmax.
4140 dstop: Stop target for the lower bound of d (default: 0 = off): both sector runs end once CC has certified
4141 dmin >= dstop, unless a lighter codeword is found (see compute_classical_distance()).
4142 wmin: Minimum distance of interest (terminate early if cw of weight <= wmin is found in RW or CC, default: 1).
4143 wmax: Maximum weight to search in CC.
4144 smax: Maximum syndrome weight for CC confinement profile.
4145 start: Expert option: list of CC start columns (int, comma-separated string "a,b,c", or
4146 sequence of ints; None or -1: all columns). CC clusters are grown only from the listed
4147 columns, and they are not limited to larger column indices. WARNING: the lower bound
4148 (and an exact result) is valid only if a code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword
4149 to one containing a listed column (e.g., one column per block of a quasi-cyclic code);
4150 the upper bound is always valid. Results are cached under the separate key
4151 '<key>:start=a,b,c'; only dmax and codewords update the main cache record.
4152 trust_start: Expert option: accept the start-list results as valid, i.e., also merge dmin and
4153 rw_steps into the main cache record, and copy an existing exact start-list record to the
4154 main record even if no calculation is needed (default: False).
4155 cbeg / cend / noscan: Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility,
4156 but ignored with a warning to stderr (use the dist_m4ri binary directly).
4157 sort_rows: Row order of H in the binary (see run_dist_m4ri()): True sorts the rows by increasing weight
4158 (faster CC for very different row weights), False keeps their order, and None (default) leaves the
4159 binary's default (sorted for matrices; the detectors of a DEM are kept in time order). The result and
4160 the cache key do not depend on it.
4161 win_hyb: Window size of the automatic hybrid RW steps (kwin=0, n >= 500: a window on every other step; see
4162 run_dist_m4ri()); 0 (default): 256 columns for a DEM, 512 for matrices. The cache key does not depend on
4163 it.
4164 pairs: The RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, see run_dist_m4ri()): the number of random pivot rows of
4165 their buckets (0: off; -1, the default: auto). The cache key does not depend on it.
4166 ksub: Experimental, should not be used (a warning is printed to stderr for ksub > 0 with method=1 or 3):
4167 subspace dimension sampled from ker(H) in RW (default: 0, full-matrix RW).
4168 dW: Extra weight window above dmin to collect codewords.
4169 maxC: Maximum number of codewords to collect.
4170 finC: Input file with initial codewords.
4171 outC: Output file to save codewords (NZLIST format).
4172 do_cws: Whether to return extracted X and Z codewords.
4173 cache_file: Optional JSON file path for persistent distance caching. The two sectors are cached as the
4174 quantum codes (H=Hx, G=Hz) -> dZ and (H=Hz, G=Hx) -> dX (with L=Lx / L=Lz if given), i.e., they share
4175 the records of compute_quantum_distance(); CSS records written before version 0.12.0 are converted.
4176 solver: "dist_m4ri" or "codedistance".
4177 codedistance_method: Method if using codedistance library.
4178 codedistance_params: Extra parameters for codedistance library.
4179 seed: Random seed.
4180 debug: Debug bitmap: the bits in BIN_DBG_MASK for the dist_m4ri binary, and the PY_DBG_* bits.
4181 verbose: Verbose reporting flag.
4182
4183 Returns:
4184 tuple (dist, dX_info, dZ_info, cws_X, cws_Z) if do_cws
4185 else (dist, dX_info, dZ_info)
4186
4187 Raises:
4188 ValueError: if Hx or Hz is missing or empty; use compute_quantum_distance() for one sector, or
4189 compute_classical_distance() for a classical code.
4190 TypeError: for an unknown keyword argument (e.g., a misspelled option).
4191 """
4192 def _nonempty(M: Any) -> bool:
4193 return M is not None and (isinstance(M, (str, Path)) or (hasattr(M, 'shape') and M.shape[0] > 0))
4194
4195 if not (_nonempty(Hx) and _nonempty(Hz)):
4196 raise ValueError(
4197 "compute_css_distance() requires both Hx and Hz (file names, or matrices with at least one row); "
4198 "use compute_quantum_distance() for one sector, or compute_classical_distance() for a classical code."
4199 )
4200
4201 eff_dmin = dmin if dmin > 0 else d_min
4202 eff_dmax = dmax if dmax > 0 else d_max # an upper bound on d = min(dX, dZ), not on either sector
4203 _check_kwargs(compute_css_distance, kwargs)
4204 start_list = _prepare_start_option(start, trust_start, noscan, cbeg, cend, solver)
4205 _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub, method, solver)
4206
4207 if solver == "codedistance":
4208 if do_cws or outC:
4209 raise ValueError("Codeword extraction is not supported with codedistance solver; use solver='dist_m4ri'.")
4210 codedistance = _get_codedistance()
4211 import numpy as np
4212 params = dict(codedistance_params or {})
4213 if num_steps is not None and "iterCount" not in params:
4214 params["iterCount"] = num_steps
4215
4216 Hx_mat = Hx.toarray() if hasattr(Hx, 'toarray') else (
4217 np.asarray(Hx, dtype=np.int8) if isinstance(Hx, (np.ndarray, list)) else None
4218 )
4219 Hz_mat = Hz.toarray() if hasattr(Hz, 'toarray') else (
4220 np.asarray(Hz, dtype=np.int8) if isinstance(Hz, (np.ndarray, list)) else None
4221 )
4222 sector_d: Dict[str, int] = {}
4223 sector_info: Dict[str, List[int]] = {}
4224 for s in ("Z", "X"):
4225 res_s = codedistance.CSScodeDistance(
4226 Hx_mat, Hz_mat, method=codedistance_method, params=params.copy(),
4227 component=s, seed=seed if seed != 0 else None
4228 )
4229 sector_d[s] = res_s.get("d", -1)
4230 sector_info[s] = format_bounds_list(sector_d[s], sector_d[s], 0) if sector_d[s] > 0 else [0, 0, 0]
4231 d_z, d_x = sector_d["Z"], sector_d["X"]
4232 dist = min(d_z, d_x) if (d_z > 0 and d_x > 0) else max(d_z, d_x)
4233 return (dist, sector_info["X"], sector_info["Z"])
4234
4235 # Solver is native multithreaded dist_m4ri: the two sectors are quantum codes, (H=Hx, G=Hz) -> dZ and
4236 # (H=Hz, G=Hx) -> dX (with L=Lx / L=Lz instead if given), with the same cache records as compute_quantum_distance().
4237 # A user dmax (a bound on min(dX, dZ)) is not an upper bound of either sector: it is passed as the stop target.
4238 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
4239 stops = [v for v in (dstop, eff_dmax) if v > 0]
4240 sector_stop = min(stops) if stops else 0
4241 need_cws = bool(do_cws or outC)
4242
4243 # Sector-specific input codewords: the files finC_X / finC_Z if they exist, otherwise finC itself
4244 finC_X, finC_Z = _css_sector_finc(finC, outC)
4245 if verbose and finC and not (finC_X or finC_Z):
4246 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Warning: finC='{finC}' (identical to outC) and its sector files are empty or "
4247 f"non-existent; silently ignoring input codewords.")
4248 if _use_distance_cache:
4249 if eff_cache_file:
4250 load_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
4251 try:
4252 if _migrate_css_records(Hx, Hz, Lx, Lz, eff_cache_file) and verbose:
4253 print("[dist_m4ri] Converted the CSS cache records written before version 0.12.0 into sector records")
4254 except Exception:
4255 pass
4256
4257 codes = _css_sector_codes(Hx, Hz, Lx, Lz)
4258 res: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
4259 for s, finC_s in (("Z", finC_Z), ("X", finC_X)):
4260 H_s, G_s, L_s = codes[s]
4261 if verbose:
4262 dual = ("Hx" if s == "X" else "Hz") if G_s is not None else ("Lz" if s == "X" else "Lx")
4263 print(f"[dist_m4ri] CSS sector d{s}: H={'Hz' if s == 'X' else 'Hx'} with "
4264 f"{'G' if G_s is not None else 'L'}={dual}")
4265 res[s] = _cached_code_distance(
4266 H_s, G_s, L_s, False, f"CSS {s}-sector", dist_m4ri=dist_m4ri, method=method, threads=threads,
4267 timeout=timeout, num_steps=num_steps, d_exp=d_exp, dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=0, dstop=sector_stop, wmin=wmin,
4268 wmax=wmax, smax=smax, start_list=start_list, dW=dW, maxC=maxC, finC=finC_s,
4269 outC=_split_css_filename(outC, s) if outC else None, need_cws=need_cws, eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file,
4270 seed=seed, debug=debug, verbose=verbose, nothrottle=nothrottle, chunk_size=chunk_size, ksub=ksub,
4271 kwin=kwin if kwin > 0 else int(kwargs.get("win", 0) or 0), win_mode=win_mode, min_hits=min_hits,
4272 cov_cws=cov_cws, refresh=refresh, trust_start=trust_start, sort_rows=sort_rows, win_hyb=win_hyb,
4273 pairs=pairs
4274 )
4275 _last_css_stats[s] = dict(_last_run_stats)
4276
4277 rx, rz = res["X"], res["Z"]
4278 dist, d_lo, d_hi, _ = _css_combine((rx["dmin"], rx["dmax"], rx["rw_steps"]),
4279 (rz["dmin"], rz["dmax"], rz["rw_steps"]), eff_dmax)
4280 if rx["cached"] and rz["cached"] and (debug & PY_DBG_CACHE) and not verbose:
4281 found = ("exact distance" if (d_lo > 0 and d_lo == d_hi) else
4282 f"dmin={d_lo} >= dstop={sector_stop}" if (sector_stop > 0 and d_lo >= sector_stop) else
4283 f"bounds dmin={d_lo}, dmax={d_hi}")
4284 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Cache hit for CSS distance ({found} known)!")
4285 if do_cws:
4286 return (dist, rx["d_info"], rz["d_info"], rx["cws"], rz["cws"])
4287 return (dist, rx["d_info"], rz["d_info"])
4288
4289
4290def _resolve_stim_dem_out_path(
4291 out_spec: Optional[Union[bool, str, Path]],
4292 circuit_src: str,
4293 mode_tag: str,
4294 ext: str,
4295 out_dir: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None
4296) -> Optional[str]:
4297 """Resolves output filepath for --out-dem or --out-stim."""
4298 if out_spec is None or out_spec is False:
4299 return None
4300 if isinstance(out_spec, str) and out_spec.strip().lower() in (
4301 "0", "false", "no", "off", "none"
4302 ):
4303 return None
4304
4305 src_path = (
4306 Path(circuit_src)
4307 if (circuit_src and circuit_src != "stim.Circuit")
4308 else None
4309 )
4310 eff_out_dir = (
4311 Path(out_dir)
4312 if out_dir is not None
4313 else (src_path.parent if src_path is not None else Path("."))
4314 )
4315
4316 is_auto = (out_spec is True) or (
4317 isinstance(out_spec, str)
4318 and out_spec.strip().lower() in ("", "1", "true", "yes", "auto")
4319 )
4320 if is_auto:
4321 if src_path is not None:
4322 stem = src_path.stem
4323 if stem.endswith("_full") or stem.endswith("_simp"):
4324 stem = stem[:-5]
4325 else:
4326 stem = "circuit"
4327 out_path = eff_out_dir / f"{stem}{mode_tag}{ext}"
4328 else:
4329 spec_str = str(out_spec)
4330 spec_path = Path(spec_str)
4331 if not spec_path.is_absolute() and os.path.dirname(spec_str) == "":
4332 out_path = eff_out_dir / spec_path
4333 else:
4334 out_path = spec_path
4335
4336 parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(str(out_path)))
4337 if parent_dir:
4338 os.makedirs(parent_dir, exist_ok=True)
4339 return str(out_path)
4340
4341
4342def _circuit_dem(circuit: Any) -> Tuple[Any, bool, bool]:
4343 """
4344 The DEM of a Stim circuit: with decompose_errors=True if stim can decompose its errors (otherwise without). An
4345 error channel with disjoint cases which stim cannot write as independent error mechanisms (e.g., a PAULI_CHANNEL_1
4346 with X and Z but no Y errors, PAULI_CHANNEL_2, or ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR) needs approximate_disjoint_errors=True,
4347 which is used only if the conversion fails without it: it only changes the probabilities of the error mechanisms,
4348 not which errors are possible (so neither the distance, unless pmin > 0, nor the codewords).
4349
4350 Returns:
4351 (dem, decompose_errors, approximate_disjoint_errors): the DEM, and the options used.
4352 """
4353 error: Optional[Exception] = None
4354 for approx in (False, True):
4355 for decomp in (True, False):
4356 try:
4357 return circuit.detector_error_model(decompose_errors=decomp, approximate_disjoint_errors=approx), \
4358 decomp, approx
4359 except Exception as e: # (stim raises ValueError)
4360 error = e
4361 assert error is not None
4362 raise error
4363
4364
4365def _warn_disabled_simple_full(simple: Optional[bool] = None, full: Optional[bool] = None, cli: bool = False) -> None:
4366 """
4367 Writes a warning to stderr if the options simple or full (CLI: --simple, --full) are given: they are disabled since
4368 version 0.13.0 (accepted for backward compatibility, but ignored). The DEM of a Stim circuit always has all
4369 detectors, and the binary drops detectors if this is exact (drop=auto, the default; e.g., the minority-basis
4370 detectors of a CSS circuit, which the simple mode stripped): as fast, with the distance of the full DEM (the
4371 simplified DEM only gives a lower bound when dropping them is not exact).
4372 """
4373 names = [f"--{n}" if cli else f"{n}=" for n, v in (("simple", simple), ("full", full)) if v is not None]
4374 if names:
4375 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: {', '.join(names)}: disabled since version 0.13.0, ignored: the DEM of a Stim "
4376 f"circuit has all detectors, and the binary drops detectors if this is exact (drop=auto, the "
4377 f"default, e.g., the minority-basis detectors of a CSS circuit; drop=0 keeps them)\n")
4378
4379
4380def _dem_from_input(
4381 dem: Optional[Any],
4382 circuit: Optional[Any],
4383 basis: Optional[str] = None,
4384 rounds: Optional[int] = None,
4385 p_noise: float = 0.001,
4386 out_dir: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
4387 out_dem: Optional[Union[bool, str, Path]] = None,
4388 out_stim: Optional[Union[bool, str, Path]] = None,
4389 circ_verbose: bool = False,
4390 drop_out: Optional[List[int]] = None,
4391 force_noise: bool = False
4392) -> Tuple[Any, Optional[Any], Optional[str]]:
4393 """
4394 The DEM of compute_dem_distance() (also used by get_cached_distance() for the cache key). A DEM
4395 (stim.DetectorErrorModel or .dem file) is used as given. A Stim circuit (stim.Circuit or .stim file, also when
4396 given as `dem`) is processed: the empty detectors are removed, the qubits are classified, the REPEAT count is set
4397 (rounds), and circuit-level noise of strength p_noise is added to a noiseless circuit (see add_noise(); none for
4398 p_noise=0), or with force_noise=True replaces the noise of the circuit (see strip_noise(); with p_noise=0, all noise
4399 is removed); then it is converted to a DEM (with all detectors). The processed circuit and the DEM are saved if
4400 requested (out_stim, out_dem, out_dir; see compute_dem_distance()). For a CSS circuit, the list drop_out (if given)
4401 is extended by the minority-basis detectors (0-based detectors of the DEM, see strip_minority_detectors()), which
4402 the binary drops if this is exact (drop=css, passed as drop=FILE). The qubits are only classified for drop_out and
4403 circ_verbose.
4404
4405 Returns:
4406 (dem, circuit, saved_dem_path): the DEM (object or file name), the processed circuit (None for a DEM input),
4407 and the file to which the DEM was saved (None if it was not saved).
4408 """
4409 if dem is not None and circuit is not None:
4410 sys.stderr.write("# Warning: both 'dem' and 'circuit' were given; using 'dem' (the circuit is ignored).\n")
4411 circuit = None
4412 if dem is not None and isinstance(dem, (str, Path)) and str(dem).endswith(".stim"):
4413 circuit = dem
4414 dem = None
4415
4416 if rounds is not None and circuit is None:
4417 raise ValueError(
4418 "--rounds option is only supported for Stim circuit (.stim) inputs."
4419 )
4420
4421 saved_dem_path: Optional[str] = None
4422 if dem is None and circuit is not None:
4423 circuit_src = str(circuit) if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)) else "stim.Circuit"
4424 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)):
4425 stim = _get_stim()
4426 circuit = stim.Circuit.from_file(str(circuit))
4427 if not hasattr(circuit, 'detector_error_model'):
4428 raise ValueError("Provided circuit object does not have detector_error_model() method.")
4429 has_rep = False
4430 if rounds is not None:
4431 if rounds < 0:
4432 raise ValueError(f"Invalid rounds={rounds}; must be >= 0.")
4433 has_rep = has_repeat_block(circuit)
4434 if not has_rep:
4435 sys.stderr.write(
4436 f"# Warning: Circuit '{circuit_src}' does not contain a "
4437 f"REPEAT block; ignoring rounds={rounds}.\n"
4438 )
4439
4440 circuit, empty_removed = remove_empty_detectors(circuit)
4441 if empty_removed > 0 and circ_verbose:
4442 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Removed {empty_removed} empty DETECTOR(s) from '{circuit_src}'")
4443
4444 filepath_hint = circuit_src if circuit_src != "stim.Circuit" else None
4445 t_res: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None # the classification of the qubits (only for drop=css and verbose)
4446 if circ_verbose or drop_out is not None:
4447 t_res = classify_qubits_thorough(circuit, verbose=False, basis_arg=basis, filepath=filepath_hint)
4448
4449 if rounds is not None and has_rep:
4450 circuit = set_circuit_rounds(circuit, rounds)
4451
4452 n_minority = None
4453 if t_res is not None and t_res["is_css"] and drop_out is not None:
4454 # the minority-basis detectors, for the exact reduction of the DEM in the binary (drop=css)
4455 mask: List[bool] = []
4456 strip_minority_detectors(circuit, t_res["basis"], verbose=False, thorough=True, thorough_res=t_res,
4457 mask_out=mask)
4458 if len(mask) == circuit.num_detectors:
4459 drop_out.extend(i for i, s in enumerate(mask) if s)
4460 n_minority = sum(mask)
4461 elif circ_verbose:
4462 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Warning: {len(mask)} detectors classified, but the circuit has "
4463 f"{circuit.num_detectors}; no detectors to drop")
4464
4465 mode_tag = "_full" # (the default names of the saved files, see _resolve_stim_dem_out_path())
4466
4467 if circ_verbose and t_res is not None:
4468 is_css_circ, is_rot_css = t_res["is_css"], t_res.get("is_rotated_css", False)
4469 css_type = "rotated-CSS (e.g. XZZX)" if is_rot_css else ("CSS" if is_css_circ else "non-CSS")
4470 rot_info = f", rotated_data={len(t_res.get('rotated_data_qubits', []))}" if is_rot_css else ""
4471 rnd_cnt = count_circuit_rounds(circuit)
4472 print(
4473 f"[dist_m4ri] Circuit basis tracking: type={css_type}, "
4474 f"basis={t_res['basis']}, data={len(t_res['data_qubits'])}, "
4475 f"X_anc={len(t_res['x_ancillas'])}, "
4476 f"Z_anc={len(t_res['z_ancillas'])}, "
4477 f"routing={len(t_res['routing_qubits'])}{rot_info}, "
4478 f"rounds={rnd_cnt}"
4479 )
4480 minority = (f", minority-basis={n_minority} (drop=css: the binary drops them if this is exact)"
4481 if n_minority is not None else "")
4482 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Circuit detectors: {circuit.num_detectors}{minority}")
4483
4484 if force_noise: # the noise of the circuit is replaced (p_noise=0: removed)
4485 noise_msg = (f"replaced the noise by circuit-level noise (p={p_noise})" if p_noise > 0.0 else
4486 "removed all noise (p_noise=0)")
4487 circuit = add_noise(circuit, p=p_noise, force=True)
4488 elif has_noise(circuit):
4489 noise_msg = "existing noise detected"
4490 elif p_noise > 0.0:
4491 noise_msg = f"added circuit-level noise (p={p_noise})"
4492 circuit = add_noise(circuit, p=p_noise)
4493 else:
4494 noise_msg = "no noise added (p_noise=0)"
4495
4496 stim_out_path = _resolve_stim_dem_out_path(out_stim, circuit_src, mode_tag, ".stim", out_dir=out_dir)
4497 if stim_out_path is not None:
4498 circuit.to_file(stim_out_path)
4499 if circ_verbose:
4500 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Saved Stim circuit to '{stim_out_path}'")
4501
4502 dem, decomp_used, approx_used = _circuit_dem(circuit)
4503 if circ_verbose:
4504 approx_msg = ", approximate_disjoint_errors=True" if approx_used else ""
4505 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Converted '{circuit_src}' to DEM ({noise_msg}, decompose_errors={decomp_used}"
4506 f"{approx_msg})")
4507 if all(hasattr(dem, a) for a in ("num_detectors", "num_observables", "num_errors")):
4508 print(
4509 f"[dist_m4ri] DEM size: {dem.num_detectors} detectors, {dem.num_observables} observables, "
4510 f"{dem.num_errors} error mechanisms"
4511 )
4512
4513 dem_out_path = _resolve_stim_dem_out_path(out_dem, circuit_src, mode_tag, ".dem", out_dir=out_dir)
4514 if dem_out_path is not None:
4515 _write_dem_file(dem, dem_out_path)
4516 saved_dem_path = dem_out_path
4517 if circ_verbose:
4518 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Saved DEM to '{dem_out_path}'")
4519 elif dem is not None and out_dem is not None and out_dem is not False:
4520 dem_src = str(dem) if isinstance(dem, (str, Path)) else "stim.Circuit"
4521 dem_out_path = _resolve_stim_dem_out_path(out_dem, dem_src, "_full", ".dem", out_dir=out_dir)
4522 if dem_out_path is not None:
4523 if isinstance(dem, (str, Path)) and os.path.exists(str(dem)):
4524 if os.path.abspath(str(dem)) != os.path.abspath(dem_out_path):
4525 shutil.copyfile(str(dem), dem_out_path)
4526 else:
4527 _write_dem_file(dem, dem_out_path)
4528 saved_dem_path = dem_out_path
4529 if circ_verbose:
4530 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Saved DEM to '{dem_out_path}'")
4531
4532 if dem is None:
4533 raise ValueError("Either 'dem' or 'circuit' must be provided.")
4534 return dem, circuit, saved_dem_path
4535
4536
4537def compute_dem_distance(
4538 dem: Optional[Any] = None,
4539 circuit: Optional[Any] = None,
4540 dist_m4ri: Optional[str] = None,
4541 method: int = 3,
4542 threads: Optional[int] = None,
4543 timeout: float = 60.0,
4544 num_steps: Optional[int] = None,
4545 d_exp: int = 0,
4546 d_min: int = 0,
4547 d_max: int = 0,
4548 dmin: int = 0,
4549 dmax: int = 0,
4550 dstop: int = 0,
4551 wmin: int = 1,
4552 wmax: int = 0,
4553 smax: Optional[int] = None,

4555 cbeg: Optional[int] = None,
4556 cend: Optional[int] = None,

4558 dW: int = -1,

4571 codedistance_method: str = "UndetectableErrorStim",

4598) -> Tuple[Any, ...]:
4599 """
4600 Computes minimum graph/hypergraph distance of a Stim Detector Error Model (DEM).
4601
4602 Args:
4603 dem: stim.DetectorErrorModel object or path to .dem / .stim file.
4604 circuit: stim.Circuit object or path to .stim file (converted to DEM; if stim cannot write an error channel with
4605 disjoint cases, e.g., a PAULI_CHANNEL_1 without Y errors, as independent error mechanisms, with
4606 approximate_disjoint_errors=True, which only changes the probabilities of the error mechanisms).
4607 dist_m4ri: Path to dist_m4ri executable (optional).
4608 method: Solver method (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing default).
4609 threads: Maximum number of worker threads (default: all logical CPUs available; subject to throttling).
4610 timeout: Execution timeout in seconds.
4611 num_steps: Maximum RW steps.
4612 d_exp: Expected distance estimate.
4613 d_min / dmin: Known lower bound on distance, inclusive.
4614 d_max / dmax: Known upper bound on distance, inclusive.
4615 dstop: Stop target for the lower bound (see compute_classical_distance(); default: 0 = off).
4616 wmin: Minimum distance of interest (terminate early if cw of weight <= wmin is found in RW or CC, default: 1).
4617 wmax: Maximum weight to search in CC.
4618 smax: Maximum syndrome weight for CC confinement profile.
4619 start: Expert option: list of CC start columns (int, comma-separated string "a,b,c", or
4620 sequence of ints; None or -1: all columns). CC clusters are grown only from the listed
4621 columns, and they are not limited to larger column indices. WARNING: the lower bound
4622 (and an exact result) is valid only if a code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword
4623 to one containing a listed column (e.g., one column per block of a quasi-cyclic code);
4624 the upper bound is always valid. Results are cached under the separate key
4625 '<key>:start=a,b,c'; only dmax and codewords update the main cache record.
4626 trust_start: Expert option: accept the start-list results as valid, i.e., also merge dmin and
4627 rw_steps into the main cache record, and copy an existing exact start-list record to the
4628 main record even if no calculation is needed (default: False).
4629 cbeg / cend / noscan: Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility,
4630 but ignored with a warning to stderr (use the dist_m4ri binary directly).
4631 sort_rows: Row order of H in the binary (see run_dist_m4ri()): True sorts the rows by increasing weight
4632 (faster CC for very different row weights), False keeps their order, and None (default) leaves the
4633 binary's default (sorted for matrices; the detectors of a DEM are kept in time order). The result and
4634 the cache key do not depend on it.
4635 win_hyb: Window size of the automatic hybrid RW steps (kwin=0, n >= 500: a window on every other step; see
4636 run_dist_m4ri()); 0 (default): 256 columns for a DEM, 512 for matrices. The cache key does not depend on
4637 it.
4638 pairs: The RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, see run_dist_m4ri()): the number of random pivot rows of
4639 their buckets (0: off; -1, the default: auto). The cache key does not depend on it.
4640 ksub: Experimental, should not be used (a warning is printed to stderr for ksub > 0 with method=1 or 3):
4641 subspace dimension sampled from ker(H) in RW (default: 0, full-matrix RW).
4642 dW: Extra weight window above dmin to collect codewords.
4643 maxC: Maximum number of codewords to collect (with expand=True, also the maximum number of codewords of the
4644 expanded list returned and written to outC; a warning is printed to stderr if some are dropped).
4645 pmin: Probability cutoff for error mechanisms in DEM.
4646 Note: CC start columns (start) and the codewords (finC, outC, do_cws) index the error mechanisms in
4647 their order of appearance in the (flattened) DEM, after the pmin cutoff: with another pmin, the columns
4648 (and the codewords) change.
4649 merge: Merge the equal columns of the DEM (error mechanisms with the same detectors and observables) in the
4650 binary (default: True). Exact: dropping two equal columns of a codeword gives a lighter one, so the
4651 distance does not change (and the cache key does not depend on merge). Column indices (finC, outC,
4652 start, the returned codewords) are those of the DEM; the codewords found use the first one of each set
4653 of equal columns (merge=False: all columns are kept, e.g., to enumerate the codewords with each of them;
4654 or expand=True to expand the list found).
4655 expand: If True, the codewords returned and written to outC are expanded in Python: each codeword is listed
4656 once for every choice among equal columns (default: False; see _expand_equal_columns()). The binary
4657 and the cache keep the merged list. With dW <= 1, the expanded list is that of merge=False (with
4658 dW >= 2, merge=False also lists lighter codewords with two equal columns added). The expanded list can
4659 be much longer (it grows quickly with the weight); with maxC > 0, it is cut at maxC codewords.
4660 drop: The detectors which the binary drops if this is verified to be exact, so that the distance (and every
4661 codeword found) is that of the DEM, found from the DEM without these detectors and the errors touching
4662 them (fewer detectors and errors: as fast as the DEM with only the primary-basis detectors of a CSS
4663 circuit). None, True, 1, or "auto" (default): the binary searches for the largest such set in the DEM alone
4664 (drop=auto, see the README), e.g., the minority-basis detectors of a CSS circuit (with the usual noise).
4665 "css": for a Stim circuit classified as CSS, its minority-basis detectors (see strip_minority_detectors()),
4666 passed as a file (otherwise, e.g., for a DEM, drop=auto is used, with a warning). False or 0: no detectors
4667 are dropped. A file name: the file with the detectors to drop (0-based, k for Dk; see read_drop_file()),
4668 for any DEM. With "css" or a file, if dropping the detectors is not exact, a note is printed to stderr and
4669 the full DEM is used. The codewords found use only the errors touching no dropped detector.
4670 outD: File to which the binary writes the detectors dropped (0-based, see read_drop_file()); with a cached
4671 result, the binary is run only to find them (with dmin = dmax: no search).
4672 out_reduced: True or a prefix PREFIX: writes the DEM without the detectors dropped (see outD) to
4673 PREFIX_red.dem, and the maps to the original DEM (its detectors and errors) to PREFIX_red.json, see
4674 write_reduced_dem() (True: PREFIX = <basename>, in out_dir or the directory of the input file).
4675 finC: Input file with initial codewords.
4676 outC: Output file to save codewords (NZLIST format).
4677 do_cws: Whether to return extracted error mechanisms / codewords.
4678 cache_file: Optional JSON file path for persistent distance caching.
4679 solver: "dist_m4ri" or "codedistance".
4680 codedistance_method: Method if using codedistance library.
4681 codedistance_params: Extra parameters for codedistance library.
4682 seed: Random seed.
4683 debug: Debug bitmap: the bits in BIN_DBG_MASK for the dist_m4ri binary, and the PY_DBG_* bits.
4684 verbose: Verbose reporting flag.
4685 simple / full: Disabled since version 0.13.0 (accepted for backward compatibility, but ignored with a warning
4686 to stderr): the DEM of a Stim circuit always has all detectors, and the minority-basis detectors of a CSS
4687 circuit (which simple=True stripped) are dropped by the binary if this is exact (see drop). The distance
4688 of the simplified circuit (a lower bound) can still be found by passing the circuit stripped with
4689 strip_minority_detectors().
4690 basis: Optional primary memory basis override ('X' or 'Z') for .stim circuits, only used with drop="css" (the
4691 other basis is that of the minority-basis detectors) and for the verbose report of the classification.
4692 rounds: Optional number of REPEAT rounds for .stim circuits (warns if no REPEAT block).
4693 out_dir: Optional output directory for saved DEM and/or Stim circuit files.
4694 out_dem: Optional bool or filename to save the constructed DEM (True = auto-named <basename>_full.dem). The
4695 codewords (outC, do_cws) index its error lines (in the order of the flattened DEM): save the DEM in the
4696 same run, since a DEM generated again from the circuit may differ (e.g., with another stim version); with
4697 outC but without out_dem, a warning is printed to stderr for a Stim circuit.
4698 out_stim: Optional bool or filename to save the processed (noisy, rounds-adjusted) Stim circuit
4699 (True = auto-named <basename>_full.stim).
4700 p_noise: Strength of the uniform circuit-level noise added to a noiseless Stim circuit (see add_noise();
4701 default: 0.001; 0: no noise is added, and a noiseless circuit gives no distance, with a note). The
4702 distance does not depend on it (unless pmin > 0), only on which faults are possible. A circuit with noise
4703 (a noise channel or a noisy measurement such as M(0.001), see has_noise()) is used as is, unless
4704 force_noise=True.
4705 force_noise: If True, the noise of a Stim circuit is replaced by the uniform noise of strength p_noise (see
4706 strip_noise(); with p_noise=0, all noise is removed, e.g., to save the noiseless circuit with out_stim),
4707 e.g., to compare circuits with the same noise model (default: False).
4708
4709 Returns:
4710 tuple (dist, d_info, cws) if do_cws else (dist, d_info)
4711
4712 Raises:
4713 TypeError: for an unknown keyword argument (e.g., a misspelled option).
4714 """
4715 global _last_run_stats
4716 eff_dmin = dmin if dmin > 0 else d_min
4717 eff_dmax = dmax if dmax > 0 else d_max
4718 _check_kwargs(compute_dem_distance, kwargs)
4719 start_list = _prepare_start_option(start, trust_start, noscan, cbeg, cend, solver)
4720 _warn_experimental_ksub(ksub, method, solver)
4721 _warn_disabled_simple_full(simple, full)
4722
4723 circ_verbose = verbose or bool(debug & PY_DBG_CIRCUITS) # Stim circuit to DEM conversion details
4724 if not 0.0 <= p_noise <= 0.5:
4725 raise ValueError(f"invalid p_noise={p_noise}: the noise strength must be in [0, 0.5]")
4726 drop_mode = _drop_mode(drop) # "auto", "0", "css", or a file name
4727 src_in = dem if dem is not None else circuit # (the input, for the names of the files of out_reduced)
4728 src_name = str(src_in) if isinstance(src_in, (str, Path)) else f"stim.{type(src_in).__name__}"
4729 css_list: List[int] = [] # the minority-basis detectors of a CSS circuit (drop=css)
4730 dem, circuit, saved_dem_path = _dem_from_input(
4731 dem, circuit, basis=basis, rounds=rounds, p_noise=p_noise, out_dir=out_dir, out_dem=out_dem,
4732 out_stim=out_stim, circ_verbose=circ_verbose,
4733 drop_out=css_list if (drop_mode == "css" and solver != "codedistance") else None, force_noise=force_noise
4734 )
4735 if getattr(dem, "num_errors", None) == 0: # (a stim object; e.g., a noiseless circuit with p_noise=0)
4736 sys.stderr.write("# Note: the DEM has no error mechanisms (no noise, e.g., p_noise=0 for a noiseless circuit "
4737 "or with force_noise): no distance computed\n")
4738 return (0, [0, 0, 0], []) if do_cws else (0, [0, 0, 0])
4739
4740 if solver == "codedistance":
4741 if do_cws or outC:
4742 raise ValueError("Codeword extraction is not supported with codedistance solver; use solver='dist_m4ri'.")
4743 if outD or out_reduced:
4744 sys.stderr.write("# Warning: outD and out_reduced are only used with solver='dist_m4ri'; ignored\n")
4745 codedistance = _get_codedistance()
4746 params = dict(codedistance_params or {})
4747 params.setdefault("filterCircuit", False)
4748 if num_steps is not None and "iterCount" not in params:
4749 params["iterCount"] = num_steps
4750
4751 if circuit is not None:
4752 res = codedistance.circuitDistance(
4753 circuit, method=codedistance_method, params=params,
4754 seed=seed if seed != 0 else None
4755 )
4756 else:
4757 H, L, priors = codedistance.StimDEM2HL(dem)
4758 if "priors" not in params and len(priors) > 0:
4759 params["priors"] = priors
4760 res = codedistance.codeDistance(
4761 H, L, tB=1, method=codedistance_method, params=params,
4762 seed=seed if seed != 0 else None
4763 )
4764 d = res.get("d", -1)
4765 d_info = format_bounds_list(d, d, 0) if d > 0 else [0, 0, 0]
4766 return d, d_info
4767
4768 # Solver is native multithreaded dist_m4ri (the cache key is that of the processed DEM, see get_cached_distance())
4769 if outC and circuit is not None and saved_dem_path is None:
4770 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: outC={outC}: the codewords index the error lines of the DEM generated from the "
4771 f"Stim circuit in this run (after the pmin cutoff), which is not saved; save it with "
4772 f"--out-dem (out_dem=...), since a DEM generated again later (e.g., with another stim "
4773 f"version) may not fit\n")
4774 fdem_run = saved_dem_path if (saved_dem_path is not None and os.path.exists(saved_dem_path)) else dem
4775 temp_files: List[str] = []
4776 try:
4777 fdrop = drop_mode # "auto", "0", or a file (drop=css: the minority-basis detectors written to a file)
4778 if drop_mode == "css":
4779 if css_list:
4780 fdrop = create_unique_file(extension="_drop.txt")
4781 temp_files.append(fdrop)
4782 with open(fdrop, "w") as f:
4783 f.write(f"# {len(css_list)} minority-basis detectors (drop=css)\n" +
4784 " ".join(str(r) for r in css_list) + "\n")
4785 if circ_verbose:
4786 print(f"[dist_m4ri] drop=css: the binary drops the {len(css_list)} minority-basis detectors if "
4787 f"this is exact")
4788 else:
4789 fdrop = "auto"
4790 sys.stderr.write("# Warning: drop=css: no minority-basis detectors (they are only known for a Stim "
4791 "circuit classified as CSS); using drop=auto (the detectors to drop found from the "
4792 "DEM)\n")
4793 outd_file = str(outD) if outD else None
4794 if out_reduced and outd_file is None:
4795 outd_file = create_unique_file(extension="_outD.txt")
4796 temp_files.append(outd_file)
4797 if outd_file is not None and not isinstance(fdem_run, (str, Path)): # (the same DEM file for the runs)
4798 fdem_file = create_unique_file(extension=".dem")
4799 temp_files.append(fdem_file)
4800 _write_dem_file(fdem_run, fdem_file)
4801 fdem_run = fdem_file
4802 cws_out_fn = None
4803 if expand and (do_cws or outC):
4804 def cws_out_fn(cws_in: List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]:
4805 return _expand_equal_columns(cws_in, fdem_run, pmin=pmin, maxC=maxC, verbose=verbose)
4806 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
4807 res = _cached_code_distance(
4808 None, None, None, False, "DEM", dist_m4ri=dist_m4ri, method=method, threads=threads, timeout=timeout,
4809 num_steps=num_steps, d_exp=d_exp, dmin=eff_dmin, dmax=eff_dmax, dstop=dstop, wmin=wmin, wmax=wmax,
4810 smax=smax if smax is not None else 0, start_list=start_list, dW=dW, maxC=maxC, finC=finC, outC=outC,
4811 need_cws=bool(do_cws or outC), eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, seed=seed, debug=debug, verbose=verbose,
4812 nothrottle=nothrottle, chunk_size=chunk_size, ksub=ksub,
4813 kwin=kwin if kwin > 0 else int(kwargs.get("win", 0) or 0), win_mode=win_mode, min_hits=min_hits,
4814 cov_cws=cov_cws, refresh=refresh, trust_start=trust_start, fdem=fdem_run, pmin=pmin,
4815 merge=merge, key_fn=lambda: _dem_cache_key(dem, pmin), cws_out_fn=cws_out_fn, fdrop=fdrop, outD=outd_file,
4816 sort_rows=sort_rows, win_hyb=win_hyb, pairs=pairs
4817 )
4818 ran = not res["cached"]
4819 drop_stats = _last_run_stats if ran else {}
4820 if outd_file is not None and res["cached"]: # a run only to find the detectors dropped (bounds coincide)
4821 if verbose:
4822 print("[dist_m4ri] Cached result: running the binary only for the detectors dropped (outD)")
4823 cached_stats = _last_run_stats
4824 run_dist_m4ri(dist_m4ri_path=dist_m4ri, method=2, fdem=str(fdem_run), dmin=1, dmax=1, wmax=1, threads=1,
4825 pmin=pmin, merge=merge, drop=fdrop, outD=outd_file, debug=debug & ~BIN_DBG_MASK)
4826 drop_stats, _last_run_stats = _last_run_stats, cached_stats # (the statistics of the cached result)
4827 ran = True

4830 sys.stderr.write(f"# Note: dropping {what} is not exact for this DEM ({drop_stats['drop_note']}); "
4831 f"the full DEM was used\n")

4835 with open(outd_file) as f: # the comment line: drop=css instead of the temporary file

4851 _remove_temp_files(temp_files, debug)

4856def _model_detector_groups(circuit: Any) -> Tuple[List[int], List[bool], int]:
4857 """
4858 The groups of the detectors of a Stim circuit for its code-sized model (see compute_model_lower_bound()): two
4859 detectors are in the same group if they share a measurement record other than a final data measurement. The final
4860 data measurements are the measurements in the final measurement block (after the last detector which precedes the
4861 last measurement) of qubits not measured before it, or all measurements of the final block if there are none
4862 (e.g., if every qubit is measured in each round). In a memory circuit, the groups are the chains of the detectors
4863 of the checks, linked by the measurements of their ancillas in consecutive rounds; the chain of a check of the
4864 measured basis ends with its detector of the final data measurements.
4865
4866 Returns:
4867 (group, final, num_final): the group of each detector (numbered in the order of their first detectors), for
4868 each group whether one of its detectors has a final data measurement, and the number of final data
4869 measurements.
4870 """
4871 stim = _get_stim()
4872 det_recs: List[List[int]] = [] # the measurement records of each detector (absolute indices)
4873 det_pos: List[int] = [] # its position in the flattened circuit
4874 meas_pos: List[int] = [] # the position of the instruction of each measurement record
4875 meas_qubits: List[frozenset] = [] # and its qubits
4876 for pos, inst in enumerate(circuit.flattened()):
4877 if inst.name == "DETECTOR":
4878 n = len(meas_pos)
4879 det_recs.append([n + t.value for t in inst.targets_copy() if t.is_measurement_record_target])
4880 det_pos.append(pos)
4881 elif stim.gate_data(inst.name).produces_measurements:
4882 for grp in inst.target_groups(): # (one record per group, e.g., per Pauli product of MPP)
4883 meas_pos.append(pos)
4884 meas_qubits.append(frozenset() if inst.name == "MPAD" else
4885 frozenset(t.qubit_value for t in grp if t.qubit_value is not None))
4886 last_meas = meas_pos[-1] if meas_pos else -1
4887 last_det = max((p for p in det_pos if p < last_meas), default=-1)
4888 before: Set[int] = set() # the qubits measured before the final measurement block
4889 for p, qs in zip(meas_pos, meas_qubits):
4890 if p <= last_det:
4891 before |= qs
4892 final_data = {r for r, (p, qs) in enumerate(zip(meas_pos, meas_qubits)) if p > last_det and qs and not qs & before}
4893 if not final_data: # (e.g., all qubits are measured in every round): all measurements of the final block
4894 final_data = {r for r, p in enumerate(meas_pos) if p > last_det}
4895 parent = list(range(len(det_recs)))
4896
4897 def find(a: int) -> int:
4898 while parent[a] != a:
4899 parent[a] = parent[parent[a]]
4900 a = parent[a]
4901 return a
4902
4903 first_det: Dict[int, int] = {} # the first detector of each measurement record (other than final data)
4904 for d, recs in enumerate(det_recs):
4905 for r in recs:
4906 if r not in final_data:
4907 a, b = find(d), find(first_det.setdefault(r, d))
4908 if a != b:
4909 parent[max(a, b)] = min(a, b) # (the root of a group is its first detector)
4910 ids: Dict[int, int] = {}
4911 group = [ids.setdefault(find(d), len(ids)) for d in range(len(det_recs))]
4912 final = [False] * len(ids)
4913 for d, recs in enumerate(det_recs):
4914 if any(r in final_data for r in recs):
4915 final[group[d]] = True
4916 return group, final, len(final_data)
4917
4918
4919def _model_matrices(
4920 cols: List[Tuple[Any, ...]], group: List[int], use: List[bool], num_observables: int
4921) -> Dict[str, Any]:
4922 """
4923 The matrices of a code-sized model (see compute_model_lower_bound()): one row per group of detectors with use[g]
4924 (the sum of the rows of its detectors), and one column per distinct pair (model column, observables) of the error
4925 mechanisms `cols` (see _dem_error_columns()); the errors with no effect on the rows nor on the observables are
4926 dropped.
4927
4928 Returns:
4929 dict with "H" and "L" (scipy.sparse.csr_matrix), "col_map" (the model column of each error mechanism, -1 if
4930 it is dropped), "groups" (the group of each row), and "trivial" (the error mechanisms which flip an observable
4931 but no row: then the model has a codeword of weight 1).
4932 """
4933 import numpy as np
4934 import scipy.sparse as sp
4935 index: Dict[Tuple[frozenset, frozenset], int] = {}
4936 col_map: List[int] = []
4937 trivial: List[int] = []
4938 for j, (dets, obs) in enumerate(cols):
4939 rows: Set[int] = set()
4940 for d in dets:
4941 if use[group[d]]:
4942 rows ^= {group[d]}
4943 if not rows:
4944 col_map.append(-1)
4945 if obs:
4946 trivial.append(j)
4947 continue
4948 col_map.append(index.setdefault((frozenset(rows), obs), len(index)))
4949 used = sorted({g for rows, _ in index for g in rows})
4950 row_of = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(used)}
4951 hi: List[int] = []
4952 hj: List[int] = []
4953 li: List[int] = []
4954 lj: List[int] = []
4955 for c, (rows, obs) in enumerate(index):
4956 hi.extend(row_of[g] for g in rows)
4957 hj.extend([c] * len(rows))
4958 li.extend(obs)
4959 lj.extend([c] * len(obs))
4960 H = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(hi), dtype=np.int8), (hi, hj)), shape=(len(used), len(index)))
4961 L = sp.csr_matrix((np.ones(len(li), dtype=np.int8), (li, lj)), shape=(num_observables, len(index)))
4962 return {"H": H, "L": L, "col_map": col_map, "groups": used, "trivial": trivial}
4963

4965def compute_model_lower_bound(
4966 circuit: Any,
4967 dist_m4ri: Optional[str] = None,
4968 method: int = 3,
4969 threads: Optional[int] = None,
4970 timeout: float = 60.0,
4971 num_steps: Optional[int] = None,
4972 dstop: int = 0,
4973 wmax: int = 0,
4974 minority: bool = True,
4975 pmin: float = 0.0,
4976 rounds: Optional[int] = None,
4977 p_noise: float = 0.001,
4978 force_noise: bool = False,
4979 out_model: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
4980 cache_file: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
4981 seed: int = 0,
4982 debug: int = 0,
4983 verbose: bool = False,
4984 nothrottle: bool = False,
4985 pairs: int = -1,
4986 return_info: bool = False,
4987 **kwargs
4988) -> Any:
4989 """
4990 Certified lower bound on the circuit-level distance of a Stim memory circuit from its code-sized model.
4991
4992 The model is a row reduction of the DEM (H, L) of the circuit (processed as in compute_dem_distance(), with the
4993 options rounds, p_noise, force_noise, and pmin): two detectors are linked if they share a measurement record other
4994 than a final data measurement, and each group of linked detectors gives one row, the sum of the rows of its
4995 detectors (see _model_detector_groups()). In a memory circuit, the groups are the chains of the detectors of the
4996 checks over the rounds: the chain of a check h of the measured basis telescopes to the parity of the final data
4997 measurements on its support, so that the column of an error mechanism is the syndrome of its net data error (a
4998 data error or a hook error), and the chains of the minority-basis checks (minority=True) add the net change of
4999 their values between their first and last measurements. Equal columns are merged, and the errors with no effect
5000 on the rows nor on the observables (e.g., ancilla measurement errors) are dropped; the model has a few columns per
5001 data qubit. Since every row is a sum of detector rows, every codeword x of the DEM (Hx = 0, Lx != 0) gives a model
5002 codeword of weight at most |x|: the distance of the model, as certified by CC (its dmin), is a lower bound on the
5003 distance of the DEM. It ignores the timing within the rounds, so it is not tight in general (e.g., 5 for the
5004 bb_72 circuit of distance 6). Any circuit gives a valid bound, but a useful one needs this structure; if an error
5005 flips an observable but no row, the bound is 1 (with a note to stderr).
5006
5007 The binary runs on the model with the rows of the measured-basis chains first, and then (minority=True) on the
5008 model with all rows, starting from that bound (the extra rows can only raise it): RW first, which ends as soon as
5009 it finds a model codeword of that weight (then the bound is not raised), and only otherwise with `method` (CC from
5010 dmin). The certified bound is stored as dmin in the
5011 cache record of the DEM (the same key as compute_dem_distance(); "dmin_model": the bound), so that a later
5012 compute_dem_distance() starts CC from it; the distances of the models are cached under their own keys.
5013
5014 Args:
5015 circuit: Stim memory circuit (stim.Circuit or .stim file).
5016 dist_m4ri: Path to dist_m4ri executable (optional).
5017 method: Solver method for the model (1=RW, 2=CC, 3=Bracketing default); only CC certifies a bound.
5018 threads / timeout / num_steps / seed / nothrottle / pairs: As for compute_dem_distance(), for each run of the
5019 binary (at most three).
5020 dstop: Stop target (see compute_dem_distance()): the runs end once CC has certified dmin >= dstop.
5021 wmax: Maximum weight of the CC rounds on the model (0: until the bounds meet or the timeout).
5022 minority: If True (default), the groups without a final data measurement (e.g., the chains of the
5023 minority-basis checks of a CSS circuit) are rows of the model as well.
5024 pmin: Probability cutoff for the error mechanisms of the DEM.
5025 rounds / p_noise / force_noise: The processing of the circuit, as in compute_dem_distance().
5026 out_model: If given, the model (with all rows used) is written to PREFIX_HR.mtx and PREFIX_LR.mtx.
5027 cache_file: Optional JSON file path for persistent distance caching.
5028 debug / verbose: As for compute_dem_distance().
5029 return_info: If True, return (bound, info).
5030
5031 Returns:
5032 The certified lower bound, or (bound, info) with return_info=True, where info has "d_info" (the bounds
5033 [dmin, dmax, rw_steps] of the circuit's DEM from the cache record, with dmin including the bound; [bound, 0, 0]
5034 without the cache), "model_d_info" and "measured_d_info" (the bounds of the model and of its measured-basis
5035 part, [] if not run), the sizes "rows", "cols", "rows_measured", "cols_measured", "groups", "groups_final",
5036 "detectors", "final_data", "dem_cols", "trivial" (the error mechanisms which flip an observable but no row),
5037 the model "H", "L", and "col_map" (the model column of each error mechanism of the DEM, -1 if dropped), and
5038 "files" (the files written with out_model).
5039
5040 Raises:
5041 TypeError: for an unknown keyword argument (e.g., a misspelled option).
5042 ValueError: if the input is not a Stim circuit.
5043 """
5044 global _distance_cache
5045 _check_kwargs(compute_model_lower_bound, kwargs, aliases=())
5046 if isinstance(circuit, (str, Path)) and not str(circuit).endswith(".stim"):
5047 raise ValueError(f"compute_model_lower_bound: {circuit} is not a Stim circuit (.stim): the code-sized model is "
5048 f"built from the detectors and measurements of a circuit")
5049 if not 0.0 <= p_noise <= 0.5:
5050 raise ValueError(f"invalid p_noise={p_noise}: the noise strength must be in [0, 0.5]")
5051 circ_verbose = verbose or bool(debug & PY_DBG_CIRCUITS)
5052 dem, circ, _ = _dem_from_input(None, circuit, rounds=rounds, p_noise=p_noise, circ_verbose=circ_verbose,
5053 force_noise=force_noise)
5054 info: Dict[str, Any] = {"d_info": [0, 0, 0], "model_d_info": [], "measured_d_info": [], "files": []}
5055 if getattr(dem, "num_errors", None) == 0:
5056 sys.stderr.write("# Note: the DEM has no error mechanisms (no noise, e.g., p_noise=0 for a noiseless circuit "
5057 "or with force_noise): no bound computed\n")
5058 return (0, info) if return_info else 0
5059 group, final, num_final = _model_detector_groups(circ)
5060 if len(group) != dem.num_detectors:
5061 raise ValueError(f"compute_model_lower_bound: {len(group)} detectors in the circuit, {dem.num_detectors} in "
5062 f"its DEM")
5063 cols = _dem_error_columns(dem, pmin)
5064 part = _model_matrices(cols, group, final, dem.num_observables) # the rows of the measured-basis chains
5065 full = _model_matrices(cols, group, [True] * len(final), dem.num_observables) if minority else part
5066 info.update(rows=full["H"].shape[0], cols=full["H"].shape[1], rows_measured=part["H"].shape[0],
5067 cols_measured=part["H"].shape[1], groups=len(final), groups_final=sum(final), detectors=len(group),
5068 final_data=num_final, dem_cols=len(cols), trivial=len(full["trivial"]), H=full["H"], L=full["L"],
5069 col_map=full["col_map"])
5070 if verbose:
5071 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Code-sized model: {info['rows']} x {info['cols']} ({info['rows_measured']} rows of the "
5072 f"chains with final data measurements, {info['rows'] - info['rows_measured']} other), from "
5073 f"{len(cols)} error mechanisms and {len(group)} detectors in {len(final)} groups ({num_final} final data "
5074 f"measurements)")
5075 if out_model:
5076 from scipy.io import mmwrite
5077 for name, M in (("HR", full["H"]), ("LR", full["L"])):
5078 path = f"{out_model}_{name}.mtx"
5079 parent_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
5080 os.makedirs(parent_dir, exist_ok=True)
5081 mmwrite(path, M, symmetry="general")
5082 info["files"].append(path)
5083 if verbose:
5084 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Saved the code-sized model to '{info['files'][0]}' and '{info['files'][1]}'")
5085 eff_cache_file = str(Path(cache_file).resolve()) if cache_file is not None else _distance_cache_file
5086
5087 def run(model: Dict[str, Any], dmin: int, run_method: int, wmin: int = 1) -> List[int]:
5088 # the bounds [dmin, dmax, rw_steps] of the model
5089 res = _cached_code_distance(
5090 model["H"], None, model["L"], False, "code-sized model", dist_m4ri=dist_m4ri, method=run_method,
5091 threads=threads, timeout=timeout, num_steps=num_steps, d_exp=0, dmin=dmin, dmax=0, dstop=dstop,
5092 wmin=wmin, wmax=wmax, smax=0, start_list=None, dW=-1, maxC=0, finC=None, outC=None, need_cws=False,
5093 eff_cache_file=eff_cache_file, seed=seed, debug=debug, verbose=verbose, nothrottle=nothrottle,
5094 chunk_size=0, ksub=0, kwin=0, win_mode=0, min_hits=None, cov_cws=100, refresh=0, trust_start=False,
5095 pairs=pairs)
5096 return list(res["d_info"])
5097
5098 if full["trivial"]:
5099 sys.stderr.write(f"# Note: code-sized model: {len(full['trivial'])} error mechanisms flip an observable but no "
5100 f"group of detectors (e.g., the first one, column {full['trivial'][0]} of the DEM), so that "
5101 f"the model has a codeword of weight 1: the bound is 1\n")
5102 bound = 1
5103 else:
5104 bound = 1
5105 if not part["trivial"]:
5106 info["measured_d_info"] = run(part, 0, method)
5107 bound = max(bound, info["measured_d_info"][0])
5108 info["model_d_info"] = info["measured_d_info"]
5109 if full is not part and (dstop <= 0 or bound < dstop) and (wmax <= 0 or bound <= wmax):
5110 # all rows: RW first (a model codeword of weight `bound` ends the search), then CC from the bound
5111 dmin = bound if bound > 1 else 0
5112 info["model_d_info"] = run(full, dmin, 1, wmin=bound)
5113 if method != 1 and not 0 < info["model_d_info"][1] <= bound:
5114 info["model_d_info"] = run(full, dmin, method)
5115 bound = max(bound, info["model_d_info"][0])
5116 info["d_info"] = [bound, 0, 0]
5117 if _use_distance_cache: # the bound as dmin in the cache record of the DEM
5118 if eff_cache_file:
5119 load_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
5120 key = _dem_cache_key(dem, pmin)
5121 prev = _distance_cache.get(key) or {}
5122 p_dmin, p_dmax, p_rw = (prev.get("dmin", 0) or 0), (prev.get("dmax", 0) or 0), (prev.get("rw_steps", 0) or 0)
5123 if p_dmax > 0 and bound > p_dmax:
5124 sys.stderr.write(f"# Warning: the code-sized model bound {bound} exceeds the cached upper bound "
5125 f"{p_dmax} of the DEM: not stored\n")
5126 info["d_info"] = format_bounds_list(p_dmin, p_dmax, p_rw)
5127 else:
5128 record = _sector_record(max(p_dmin, bound), p_dmax, p_rw, prev.get("cws", []))
5129 record["dmin_model"] = max(bound, prev.get("dmin_model", 0) or 0)
5130 if record != prev:
5131 _distance_cache[key] = record
5132 if eff_cache_file:
5133 save_distance_cache(eff_cache_file)
5134 info["d_info"] = list(record["d_info"])
5135 if verbose:
5136 print(f"[dist_m4ri] Code-sized model: certified lower bound d >= {bound} on the circuit distance (model bounds "
5137 f"{info['model_d_info']}; measured-basis rows only: {info['measured_d_info']})")
5138 return (bound, info) if return_info else bound
5139

5141def _write_nzlist_file(filepath: str, cws: List[List[int]]) -> None:
5142 """Writes codewords to a text file in NZLIST format (1-based indices).
5143 Skips creating the file if cws is empty.
5144 """
5145 if not cws:
5146 return
5147 with open(filepath, "w") as f:
5148 f.write("%% NZLIST\n")
5149 f.write(f"% {len(cws)} codewords\n")
5150 for cw in cws:
5151 f.write(f"{len(cw)} " + " ".join(str(idx + 1) for idx in cw) + "\n")
5152

5478 )

5619 elif val.lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "auto", ""):
5620 args["out_stim"] = True
5621 else:
5622 args["out_stim"] = val
5623 else:
5624 args["unrecognized"].append(arg)
5625
5626 i += 1
5627
5628 # Auto-infer classical mode when not explicitly set (matching src/util_io.c)
5629 if args["classical"] == -1:
5630 if (
5631 args["finG"] is not None or args["finL"] is not None

5652 nothrottle, chunk_size (batch), ksub, kwin (win), win_mode, win_hyb, pairs,

5655 --trust-start, sort_rows
5656
5657Help options:
5658 -h, --help : display help for commonly used parameters (fits 80 rows; --help TOPIC: as --morehelp TOPIC)
5659 --morehelp : display full help for all available parameters (or for TOPIC: --morehelp TOPIC)
5660 --version : display the versions of dist_m4ri.py and of the dist_m4ri binary
5661"""

5664
5665def print_cli_help(file: Optional[Any] = None) -> None:
5666 help_text = f"""dist_m4ri.py (version {__version__}): Multithreaded distance calculator Python CLI
5667Usage: dist_m4ri.py [key=val | --flag val ...]
5668
5669Input matrices & models:
5670 fdem=FILE Detector Error Model (.dem) or Stim circuit (.stim) file
5671 finH=FILE Parity check matrix H (classical) or Hx (CSS quantum) (.mmx/.mtx)
5672 finG=FILE, finL=FILE Hz check matrix or Lx logical operator matrix (quantum CSS)
5673 fin=PREFIX Base prefix for CSS matrices (loads ${{fin}}X.mtx, ${{fin}}Z.mtx, e.g. try -> tryX.mtx)
5674 Hx=FILE, Hz=FILE CSS check matrices, both required (computes dX and dZ)
5675 Lx=FILE, Lz=FILE CSS logical operators (optional, constructed if omitted)
5676 pmin=PROB Minimum error probability threshold for DEM errors (default: 0.0)
5677 merge=0|1 Merge equal DEM columns (exact; codewords use the first one) (default: 1)
5678 drop=auto|0|css|FILE DEM detectors to drop if verified exact: auto=1 (default), 0 (none), css, or a file
5679 outD=FILE Write the DEM detectors dropped (0-based) to FILE
5680 --out-reduced [PFX] Save the reduced DEM and its maps to the DEM: PFX_red.dem and PFX_red.json
5681 classical=0|1 1: classical code (Hx only), 0: quantum CSS (auto-detected)
5682 basis=X|Z Override primary memory basis ('X' or 'Z') for .stim circuits (with drop=css)
5683 --rounds [N] Set REPEAT block count in .stim circuit (default: 2; warns if no REPEAT)
5684 --out-dir DIR Output directory for saved .dem/.stim files (default: input file dir)
5685 --out-dem [FILE] Save constructed DEM (default: <basename>_full.dem)
5686 --out-stim [FILE] Save processed/noisy Stim circuit (default: <basename>_full.stim)
5687 --p-noise P Strength of the noise added to a noiseless .stim circuit (default: 0.001; 0: none)
5688 --force-noise Replace the noise of a .stim circuit by that of --p-noise (with P=0: remove it)
5689 --model-lb Certified lower bound for a .stim circuit from its code-sized model
5690
5691Method and distance bounds:
5692 method=1|2|3 1=RW (upper bound), 2=CC (lower bound/exact), 3=Bracketing (default: 3)
5693 dmin=N Certified lower bound, inclusive (CC starts from dmin) (default: 0)
5694 dmax=N Known upper bound, inclusive (CC up to w=dmax-1 only) (default: 0)
5695 dstop=N Stop once CC certifies dmin>=dstop (not an upper bound) (default: 0)
5696 dexp=N Expected distance estimate (alias: dest) (default: 0)
5697
5698Search limits and stopping criteria:
5699 steps=N Maximum RW steps / information sets (default: 100000)
5700 wmax=N Maximum cluster weight to search in CC (0=until bound/timeout)
5701 wmin=N Stop immediately if cw with weight <= wmin is found (default: 1)
5702 min_hits=N Stop RW when lowest-weight cws are hit N times on average (default: 5)
5703 timeout=SEC Execution timeout in seconds, 0 for infinite (default: 60.0)
5704
5705Multithreading & execution:
5706 threads=N Max worker threads to use (default: all logical CPUs; subject to
5707 automatic throttling unless nothrottle=1)
5708 solver=NAME Distance solver backend: 'dist_m4ri' (default) or 'codedistance'
5709
5710Codeword collection & caching:
5711 --cws Collect and output non-trivial minimum-weight codewords
5712 outC=FILE Save output codewords (for CSS, auto-suffixed _X.nz / _Z.nz)
5713 finC=FILE Input initial candidate codewords (.nz file)
5714 expand=0|1 DEM codewords: list all choices among equal columns (merge) (default: 0)
5715 cache=FILE Persistent JSON cache file (default: tmp_dist_cache.json)
5716 --no-cache / nocache Disable persistent JSON caching
5717 --verbose / -v Explain bounds, steps, cache status, and miss probability estimates
5718
5719Extra parameters (see --morehelp for details):
5720 smax=N (0) Max syndrome weight for CC confinement profile (0 to disable)
5721 start=LIST (-1) Expert: CC from listed columns only, e.g. start=0,48 (see --morehelp)
5722 --trust-start Expert: accept start-list results as valid (copied to main cache record)
5723 noscan, cbeg, cend Disabled in Python (ignored with a warning); use the dist_m4ri binary
5724 sort_rows=0|1 Sort the rows of H by weight for CC (default: 1 for matrices, 0 for a DEM)
5725 --simple, --full Disabled (ignored with a warning): the DEM has all detectors (see drop)
5726 nothrottle=1 (0) Disable automatic thread throttling (also --no-throttle)
5727 chunk_size=N (0) Max RW batch per claim (default: 0 for adaptive 25-500, alias: batch)
5728 ksub=N (0) EXPERIMENTAL, do not use: RW subspace sketch dimension (0: full matrix)
5729 kwin=N (0) RW localized window size (0: auto/hybrid for n>=500, alias: win)
5730 win_mode=0|1 (0) RW window metric: 0=Tanner graph BFS, 1=index proximity
5731 win_hyb=N (0) Hybrid RW window size (0: 256 for a DEM, 512 for matrices)
5732 pairs=N (-1) RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2; -1: auto, 0: off)
5733 cov_cws=N (100) Number of lowest-weight cws used for the min_hits statistic
5734 refresh=N (0) Periodic N basis refresh interval in RW steps (experimental ksub only)
5735 maxC=N (0) Maximum number of codewords to collect (0: unlimited)
5736 dW=N (0) Extra weight window above dmin to collect codewords
5737 seed=N (0) Random number generator seed
5738 debug=N (0) Debug bitmap, OR-combined (1: summary, 2: progress, 4: status, ...)
5739
5740Help options:
5741 -h, --help [TOPIC] Display this help message (with TOPIC: the same as --morehelp TOPIC)
5742 --morehelp [TOPIC] Display full help for all parameters (or only for TOPIC, e.g., maxC or windows)
5743 --version Display the versions of dist_m4ri.py and of the dist_m4ri binary
5744"""
5745 print(help_text, file=file)
