5747
5748def _cli_morehelp_text() -> str:
5749 """The full help text of the CLI (--morehelp)."""
5750 return f"""dist_m4ri.py (version {__version__}): Multithreaded distance calculator Python CLI
5751Usage: dist_m4ri.py [key=val | --flag val ...]
5752
5753Required input (at least one matrix/model specification):
5754 fdem=FILE Detector Error Model (.dem) or Stim circuit (.stim) file.
5755 Automatically constructs parity check H and logical L matrices. An error
5756 channel which stim cannot write as independent errors (e.g., PAULI_CHANNEL_1
5757 without Y errors) is converted with approximate_disjoint_errors=True (only the
5758 probabilities change).
5759 finH=FILE Parity check matrix file in Matrix Market (.mmx / .mtx) format.
5760 For classical codes, this is check matrix H. For CSS codes, Hx.
5761 finG=FILE Generator / Hz matrix for quantum CSS codes in Matrix Market format.
5762 finL=FILE Logical operator matrix Lx for quantum CSS codes in Matrix Market format.
5763 Note: For a quantum CSS code, either finL (Lx) or finG (Hz) is required.
5764 fin=PREFIX Base prefix for CSS matrices (loads ${{fin}}X.mtx and ${{fin}}Z.mtx, e.g. try -> tryX.mtx).
5765 Hx=FILE, Hz=FILE CSS check matrices Hx and Hz, both required: computes both dX and dZ, and
5766 d = min(dX, dZ) (finH=Hx with finG=Hz gives dZ only).
5767 Lx=FILE, Lz=FILE Alternative syntax for specifying CSS logical operator matrices.
5768 pmin=PROB Minimum error probability threshold for DEM parsing (default: 0.0).
5769 Error mechanisms with probability < pmin are filtered out. The column
5770 indices (start, finC, outC) count only the error mechanisms kept: with
5771 another pmin, the columns (and the codewords) change.
5772 merge=0|1 Merge the equal columns of the DEM (error mechanisms with the same detectors
5773 and observables) in the dist_m4ri binary (default: 1). Exact: dropping two
5774 equal columns of a codeword gives a lighter one, so the distance does not
5775 change (nor does the cache key). Column indices (finC, outC, start) are those
5776 of the DEM; the codewords found use the first one of each set of equal columns
5777 (use merge=0 to enumerate the codewords with each of them, or expand=1 to
5778 expand the list found).
5779 drop=auto|0|css|FILE The detectors which the binary drops from the DEM if this is verified to be
5780 exact (default: auto; drop=1 is the same as drop=auto; drop=0 keeps all
5781 detectors). Exact if every error touching them has a twin, an error with the
5782 same other detectors which touches none of them (or none if it has no other
5783 detector), with the same observables (or with L + A H for one matrix A):
5784 then the distance of the DEM is found from the smaller DEM without these
5785 detectors and the errors touching them, and the codewords found (outC) are
5786 codewords of the DEM which use only errors touching no dropped detector.
5787 drop=auto: the binary searches for the largest such set (with the same
5788 observables) in the DEM alone, e.g., the minority-basis detectors of a CSS
5789 circuit with the usual noise (see the README). drop=css: for a Stim circuit
5790 classified as CSS (including locally rotated CSS such as XZZX codes, by
5791 ancilla and data basis tracking), its minority-basis detectors (the basis
5792 other than the memory basis, see basis); otherwise (e.g., for a DEM),
5793 drop=auto is used, with a warning. drop=FILE: the detectors in FILE, for any
5794 DEM (a text file with the 0-based detector indices, k for Dk, separated by
5795 white space or commas; lines starting with '#' or '%' are comments; e.g.,
5796 written by outD). With css or FILE, if dropping the detectors is not exact, a
5797 note is printed and the full DEM is used. The values 0, 1, auto, and css take
5798 precedence over files with these names (write ./1 for a file named 1).
5799 outD=FILE Write the detectors dropped from the DEM by the binary to FILE (0-based, in
5800 the format of a drop file; only the comment line '# 0 of M detectors
5801 dropped ...' if none). With a cached result, the binary is run only for
5802 this (with dmin = dmax: no search).
5803 --out-reduced [PREFIX]
5804 Save the DEM without the detectors dropped (see drop and outD) to
5805 PREFIX_red.dem: the errors touching none of them (after the cutoff pmin, in
5806 the order of the flattened DEM), with the other detectors numbered
5807 consecutively. Its maps to the DEM go to PREFIX_red.json: "detectors" (the
5808 original index of each detector of the reduced DEM, i.e., those not in
5809 outD), "errors" (the original index of each error, as the columns of outC),
5810 "dropped", and "num_detectors", "num_errors", "pmin", "source", "dem",
5811 "drop" (also out_reduced=PREFIX; default PREFIX: the basename of the input
5812 file, without _full, in --out-dir or the directory of the input file). The
5813 reduced DEM has the same distance, and its codewords are mapped to
5814 codewords of the DEM by "errors".
5815 classical=0|1 Code type override:
5816 1: Classical linear code (Hx only; ignores/discards logicals).
5817 0: Quantum CSS code (requires logicals or Hz).
5818 Default: auto-detected (1 if only finH/Hx is given; 0 otherwise).
5819 --simple / --full Disabled since version 0.13.0 (also simple=1, full=1): accepted for backward
5820 compatibility, but ignored with a warning to stderr. The DEM of a Stim circuit
5821 always has all detectors: the binary drops detectors if this is exact (see
5822 drop; e.g., the minority-basis detectors which --simple stripped), which is
5823 as fast and gives the distance of the full DEM (the stripped DEM only gives a
5824 lower bound when dropping them is not exact).
5825 basis=X|Z Explicitly set primary memory basis ('X' or 'Z') for .stim circuits
5826 (default: auto-detected from filename or initial/final resets/measurements);
5827 with drop=css, the detectors of the other basis are dropped if this is exact
5828 (otherwise only used for the --verbose report; ignored with a warning).
5829 --rounds [N] Construct DEM from a .stim circuit with N repetitions in its REPEAT block
5830 (default: 2 when --rounds is given without a number; also rounds=N).
5831 Issues a warning and continues with the original circuit if no REPEAT block.
5832 --out-dir DIR Output directory for saving constructed DEM and/or processed Stim circuit
5833 files (also out_dir=DIR; default: directory of the input .stim/.dem file).
5834 --out-dem [FILE] Save constructed (flattened) DEM to FILE. If given without a filename (or
5835 out_dem=1), automatically saves as <basename>_full.dem.
5836 The codewords (outC) index its error lines: save the DEM in the same run (a DEM
5837 generated again from the circuit may differ, e.g., with another stim version).
5838 --out-stim [FILE] Save processed (noisy, rounds-adjusted) Stim circuit to FILE. If given without
5839 a filename (or out_stim=1), automatically saves as <basename>_full.stim.
5840 --p-noise P Strength p of the uniform circuit-level noise added to a noiseless Stim circuit
5841 (also p_noise=P; default: 0.001; 0: no noise is added, and then a noiseless
5842 circuit gives no distance): DEPOLARIZE2(p) after two-qubit gates (CX, CZ,
5843 XCY, SWAP, ISWAP, SQRT_XX, CXSWAP, ..., also II), DEPOLARIZE1(p/10) after
5844 one-qubit gates (I, X, H, H_XY, S, SQRT_X, C_XYZ, ...), on the qubit of a
5845 classically controlled gate (e.g., CX rec[-1] 5), and on the qubits idle since
5846 the previous TICK, and X (Z) flips with probability p after Z-basis or Y-basis
5847 (X-basis) resets and before measurements (before and after MR, MRX, MRY); the
5848 multi-qubit measurements (MPP, MXX, MYY, MZZ) and Pauli product gates (SPP,
5849 SPP_DAG) get no noise. A circuit with noise (a noise channel, or a noisy
5850 measurement such as M(0.001)) is used as is, unless --force-noise. The
5851 distance does not depend on p (unless pmin > 0), only on which faults exist.
5852 --force-noise Replace the noise of a Stim circuit (also --force or force_noise=1): all of its
5853 noise is removed (noise channels, measurement flip probabilities, heralded
5854 noise; see stim's Circuit.without_noise()), and then the uniform noise of
5855 --p-noise is added (none with --p-noise 0, e.g., to save the noiseless circuit
5856 with --out-stim), e.g., to compare circuits with the same noise model.
5857 --model-lb Certified lower bound on the distance of a Stim memory circuit (fdem=FILE.stim)
5858 from its code-sized model, instead of the distance of its DEM (also
5859 model_lb=1; see compute_model_lower_bound()): the detectors linked by shared
5860 measurements, other than the final data measurements, form chains (one per
5861 check of a memory circuit), and each chain gives a row of the model, the sum
5862 of its detector rows (the chain of a check of the measured basis telescopes
5863 to the parity of the final data measurements on the check; the chains of the
5864 minority-basis checks are rows as well), with the equal columns merged. Each
5865 codeword of the DEM gives a model codeword of no larger weight, so the model
5866 distance certified by CC is a lower bound on the circuit distance; it ignores
5867 the timing within the rounds (not tight in general, e.g., 5 for the bb_72
5868 circuit of distance 6). The binary runs on the model with the measured-basis
5869 rows, then with all rows from that bound (RW first; method, threads, timeout,
5870 steps, dstop, wmax, and seed apply to each run). The bound is stored as dmin in
5871 the cache record of the DEM, and the bounds of the circuit are printed.
5872 --out-model PREFIX With --model-lb, write the model to PREFIX_HR.mtx and PREFIX_LR.mtx (also
5873 out_model=PREFIX).
5874 (conflicting inputs) The input is selected in the order fdem, Hx/Hz (CSS code), and
5875 finH/finG/finL/fin (fin only supplies the missing finH and finG); the
5876 ignored inputs (e.g., matrices with fdem, pmin, merge, expand, drop, or outD
5877 without fdem, basis, --p-noise, or --force-noise without a Stim circuit, basis
5878 without drop=css, fin with finH, classical=1 with finG) give a warning.
5879
5880Calculation method:
5881 method=1|2|3 Calculation method (default: 3):
5882 1: Random Window (RW) algorithm (upper bound on distance).
5883 Repeatedly samples random information sets to find low-weight
5884 codewords. Fast for discovering small errors.
5885 2: Connected Cluster (CC) algorithm (lower bound / exact distance).
5886 Exhaustive cluster search finding certified lower bound dmin or
5887 exact distance if run to completion.
5888 3: Bracketing mode (concurrent RW and CC).
5889 Dynamically allocates worker threads between CC (lower bound) and
5890 RW (upper bound) to converge on the exact distance rapidly, based on
5891 the measured CC and RW times, the bounds, and the remaining timeout.
5892
5893Distance bounds and guidance:
5894 dmin=N Known certified lower bound on distance (default: 0).
5895 CC search begins at weight w = max(1, dmin).
5896 dmax=N Known upper bound on distance (default: 0).
5897 CC ends once dmin = dmax (with outC, after the rounds w = dmax..dmax+dW);
5898 RW ignores candidate codewords of weight >= dmax unless collecting codewords
5899 or needed for min_hits. For a CSS code (Hx=, Hz=), dmax is a bound on
5900 d = min(dX, dZ), not on either sector: it is used as dstop for both sectors.
5901 dstop=N Stop target for the lower bound (default: 0 = off): the search (method=2
5902 or 3) ends once CC has certified dmin >= dstop, unless a lighter codeword is
5903 found. Unlike dmax, dstop is not an upper bound and is not reported as dmax
5904 (the bounds are 'dmin w steps' with dmin >= dstop, w: the lightest codeword
5905 found, or 0); a cached lower bound dmin >= dstop answers the request without
5906 a calculation. E.g., dstop=U wmin=U-1 decides whether d >= U.
5907 dexp=N Expected code distance estimate (alias: dest) (default: 0).
5908 Hint for method=3: as long as RW has found no codeword, CC rounds at
5909 w > dexp run only on threads which cannot run RW (CC pauses if RW can
5910 use all threads); CC resumes once RW finds a codeword or ends.
5911
5912Search limits and stopping criteria:
5913 steps=N Maximum number of RW steps / information sets across all threads
5914 (default: 100000).
5915 wmax=N Maximum cluster weight to analyze in CC (default: 0 = until bound/timeout;
5916 with method=2, a known dmax is used as wmax).
5917 wmin=N Minimum distance threshold (default: 1).
5918 If a codeword of weight w <= wmin is discovered, search halts immediately
5919 (not when collecting codewords with outC or maxC).
5920 timeout=SEC Execution timeout in seconds (default: 60.0; set 0 for infinite).
5921 In method=3, it guides the CC vs RW thread balance, and a CC round predicted
5922 not to finish in time is not started while RW runs (in method=2, and with
5923 steps=0, it is started anyway: it may still find a codeword of weight dmin).
5924
5925Multithreading & throttling:
5926 threads=N Maximum number of worker threads to allocate (default: all logical CPUs
5927 available to the process, i.e., its CPU affinity mask, e.g., with taskset).
5928 Subject to automatic thread throttling unless nothrottle=1 is specified:
5929 - Small codes, methods 1 and 3 (<= 4 threads for n < 60, or for m*n < 2e4
5930 with a small RW workload m*n*steps < 5e7; otherwise <= 16 threads for
5931 n < 150 or m*n < 1e5, if m*n*steps < 2e8; m: number of rows of H).
5932 Method 2 starts 4 threads, and the others once a CC round takes longer
5933 (predicted > 2 ms on the threads started, or running for 5 ms).
5934 - Large memory matrices (above 15 MB of dense RW working memory per thread:
5935 at most 32 RW threads, within a quarter of the physical memory).
5936 - Small RW step counts (RW threads clamped to <= (steps + 9) / 10).
5937 The last two limits apply to RW threads only: CC (method=2) is not
5938 limited, and in method=3 CC rounds can use all threads.
5939 CC rounds with few start columns per thread are split into work units
5940 which also fix the first 1-3 cluster extensions (balanced load).
5941 nothrottle=1 Disable automatic thread throttling (also --no-throttle).
5942 Forces allocation of the exact number of threads requested.
5943 chunk_size=N Maximum RW batch claimed at once by a thread (default: 0 = adaptive
5944 25-500). Near the end of the steps, batches shrink to at most
5945 ceil(remaining / (4 * RW threads)) steps. Alias: batch=N.
5946 ksub=N EXPERIMENTAL, should not be used (a warning is printed): subspace sketch
5947 dimension for RW (default: 0 = full matrix).
5948 Precomputes N = ker(H) once; each thread echelonizes a compact
5949 ksub x n sampled subspace in L1/L2 cache (e.g. ksub=32 or 64).
5950 Automatically falls back to ksub=0 with a warning if m < nu = dim(ker H).
5951 Each step reduces the span of ksub distinct rows of N, so that a few
5952 codewords are found much more often than others, and min_hits may end
5953 RW early.
5954 kwin=N Localized column permutation window size W around a random seed
5955 column j0, used in every RW step (alias: win=N). Default: 0 = automatic
5956 hybrid for n>=500: every other step uses an index window (win_mode=1) of
5957 win_hyb columns, and the other steps uniform random permutations (also
5958 for codewords which are not local in the column order).
5959 win_mode=0|1 Locality metric for kwin > 0: 0 = Tanner graph BFS neighbors
5960 (default), 1 = contiguous column index window.
5961 win_hyb=N Window size of the hybrid RW steps (kwin=0, n>=500; at most 3n/4).
5962 Default: 0 = 256 columns for a DEM, 512 for matrices. The window
5963 columns come first in the elimination order; in a DEM, they are errors
5964 close in time, which touch few detectors: windows of 192-256 columns find
5965 circuit codewords 2-10 times faster than 512, and windows of one round of
5966 columns much slower. With --verbose (or debug&1), the binary prints the
5967 rounds of a DEM (estimated from the time translation of its errors: D
5968 detectors and L columns per round) and the codewords found by the
5969 uniform and by the window steps.
5970 pairs=N RW pairs of non-pivot columns (p=2, as in Lee-Brickell and Stern): a RW
5971 step also finds the codewords with exactly two non-pivot columns,
5972 checking only the pairs of columns which agree on N random pivot rows
5973 (at most 64; 0 = off). Default: -1 = auto, about one non-pivot column per
5974 bucket, with fewer rows while a codeword of the weight of the upper bound
5975 would be kept with probability below 0.8. The pairs find the
5976 minimum-weight codewords of circuit DEMs 7-25 times faster, and lighter
5977 codewords of codes with a large distance. Not with ksub. With --verbose
5978 (or debug&1), the binary prints the pairs checked per step and the
5979 codewords found by pairs and by single columns.
5980 min_hits=N QDistRnd-style RW stopping criterion (default: 5, 0 = disabled).
5981 Stops RW when the average number of times <n> that RW has found each
5982 codeword reaches min_hits, both for the codewords of the minimum weight
5983 found and for a representative set of cov_cws lowest-weight codewords
5984 (heavier codewords are kept until enough lighter ones are found). A
5985 single codeword suffices. A lighter codeword is missed with probability
5986 about exp(-<n>), assuming that lighter codewords are found at least as
5987 often. With debug&1 (or --verbose), a warning is printed at the end if
5988 the hit counts of codewords of the same weight are strongly non-uniform
5989 (then exp(-<n>) is optimistic), together with an information-set estimate
5990 (uniform random information sets) of the probability to miss a lighter
5991 codeword and of the RW steps needed for 1%. With --verbose, both
5992 estimates are always shown for a result which is not certified.
5993 cov_cws=N Size of the representative set of lowest-weight codewords for min_hits
5994 (default: 100; 0 = only the minimum weight). Without outC and maxC, at
5995 most cov_cws minimum-weight codewords are tracked (all if cov_cws=0).
5996 With fewer minimum-weight codewords, a smaller cov_cws may stop RW
5997 earlier.
5998 refresh=N Periodic adaptive basis refresh interval in RW steps, only with the
5999 experimental ksub > 0 (default: 5000 when ksub > 0, 0 to disable).
6000 Re-echelonizes N and substitutes heavier basis rows with discovered
6001 min-weight codewords.
6002
6003Connected Cluster (CC) search options:
6004 smax=N Maximum syndrome weight for confinement profile (default: 0).
6005 When smax > 0, tracks minimum syndrome weights for each error weight.
6006 When smax=0, confinement is not computed.
6007 sort_rows=0|1 Sort the rows of H by increasing weight (stable) in the dist_m4ri binary
6008 (default: the binary's, 1 for matrices and 0 for a DEM). CC extends a
6009 cluster by the columns of the first row of its syndrome (in row order), so
6010 that light rows first reduce the CC work for matrices with very different
6011 row weights (e.g., 1.7-4x with the hook columns of an extended CSS
6012 distance). The detectors of a DEM are in time order, which is better for
6013 CC: use sort_rows=0 also for matrices exported from a DEM. The distance, RW,
6014 and the cache key do not depend on the order of the rows; CC enumerates the
6015 same codewords (outC), possibly in another order and with other hit counts.
6016 start=LIST Expert option: comma-separated list of CC start columns (0-based), e.g.,
6017 start=0,48,96 (default: -1 = all columns; start=N is a one-element list).
6018 CC clusters are grown only from the listed columns, and they are NOT
6019 limited to larger column indices. Use, e.g., one column per block of a
6020 quasi-cyclic code. WARNING: dmin (and an exact result) is valid only if a
6021 code symmetry maps every minimum-weight codeword to one containing a listed
6022 column; dmax is always valid. For DEM input, columns index the error
6023 mechanisms in their order in the (flattened) DEM, after the pmin cutoff.
6024 Results are cached under a separate key '<key>:start=a,b,c'; only dmax and
6025 codewords are merged into the main cache record. (Before version 0.10.0,
6026 start=N limited CC to clusters started at column N using only larger
6027 columns; this is now cbeg=N cend=N of the dist_m4ri binary.)
6028 --trust-start Expert option (also trust_start=1): accept the start-list results as valid,
6029 i.e., also merge dmin and rw_steps into the main cache record, and copy an
6030 existing exact start-list record to the main record even if no calculation
6031 is needed. Only use it if the code symmetry assumption above holds.
6032 noscan, cbeg, cend Disabled in the Python interface: accepted for backward compatibility, but
6033 ignored with a warning to stderr. These expert options of the dist_m4ri
6034 binary do not give valid bounds on their own: noscan=1 runs CC only at
6035 weight w=wmax (method=2); cbeg/cend limit CC start columns to a range for
6036 split runs, where every column is eventually covered by one of the runs.
6037 Run the dist_m4ri binary directly to use them (see its --morehelp).
6038
6039Codeword collection and export:
6040 --cws Collect and display non-trivial minimum-weight codewords.
6041 outC=FILE Export found codewords of weight up to min_w + dW (min_w: minimum weight
6042 found) to file in .nz format. In method=2/3, once the distance d is
6043 known, CC rounds w = d..d+dW enumerate all such codewords (unless the
6044 timeout is hit; for a DEM, up to the choice of equal columns: see merge).
6045 In CSS mode, automatically saves X-codewords to FILE_X.nz and
6046 Z-codewords to FILE_Z.nz. The codewords of the run are merged with the
6047 cached ones; with finC=FILE (the same file), those already in FILE are kept.
6048 finC=FILE Import initial candidate codewords from file in .nz format.
6049 In CSS mode, automatically resolves FILE_X.nz and FILE_Z.nz.
6050 maxC=N Maximum number of codewords to collect (default: 0 = unlimited); with
6051 expand=1, also the maximum number of codewords of the expanded list.
6052 dW=N Extra weight window above minimum distance to collect codewords
6053 (w <= min_w + dW) (default: 0).
6054 expand=0|1 Python only, for a DEM: list each codeword found once for every choice
6055 among equal columns, which the binary merges (see merge; default: 0). The
6056 binary and the cache keep the merged list. With dW <= 1, the expanded list
6057 is that of merge=0 (with dW >= 2, merge=0 also lists lighter codewords with
6058 two equal columns added). The list grows quickly with the weight: with
6059 maxC > 0, at most maxC codewords are written (a warning if some are dropped).
6060 (DEM codewords) The indices refer to the error lines of the DEM in the order of the flattened
6061 DEM, after the pmin cutoff. For a Stim circuit, save the DEM with --out-dem in
6062 the same run (a warning is printed otherwise): a DEM generated again from the
6063 circuit may differ (e.g., with another stim version).
6064
6065Distance caching (Python CLI):
6066 cache=FILE Path to persistent JSON cache file (default: tmp_dist_cache.json).
6067 --no-cache / nocache Disable reading and writing to the persistent JSON cache.
6068
6069General options:
6070 solver=NAME Distance calculation engine: 'dist_m4ri' (default) or 'codedistance'.
6071 --verbose / -v Enable verbose output with detailed explanations of bounds,
6072 timings, steps, and cache status (implies the debug bits 1, 2,
6073 65536, and 131072). For a RW upper bound which is not certified,
6074 also estimates the probability that a lighter codeword was missed
6075 (from the average hits <n>, and from uniform random information sets
6076 with n, rank(H), and the RW steps), with the RW steps and time needed
6077 for a 1% miss probability.
6078 seed=N Random number generator seed (default: 0; the binary replaces seed<=0 by
6079 time(NULL) + 10*pid - 1000*seed).
6080 debug=N Debug bitmap (default: 0), a decimal or hexadecimal (0x...) integer;
6081 multiple debug arguments are OR-combined. Bits 1 to 32768 are passed
6082 to the dist_m4ri binary, which prints diagnostic output to stderr (see
6083 its --morehelp; lower bits are more informative):
6084 1: summary (input matrices, rounds of a DEM, RW windows, stop reason,
6085 codeword statistics, codewords found by each kind of RW step),
6086 2: progress (run plan, finished CC rounds, new upper bounds),
6087 4: periodic status (after 1, 2, 4, ... s, then every 60 s),
6088 8: thread allocation and timing, 16: code parameters (ranks, k),
6089 32: codeword supports, 64: arguments, 128: matrices,
6090 256: codeword dump, 2048: no size cutoff.
6091 Bits 65536 and above are used by the Python wrapper only:
6092 65536: dist_m4ri command lines and run times,
6093 131072: cache messages,
6094 262144: Stim circuit to DEM conversion details,
6095 524288: keep (and list) the temporary files.
6096
6097Option groups (--help GROUP prints all entries of GROUP):
6098 windows kwin, win_mode, win_hyb
6099 stopping, stop steps, wmin, timeout, min_hits, cov_cws
6100 bounds dmin, dmax, dstop, dexp, wmax
6101 dem fdem, pmin, merge, drop, outD, --out-reduced, expand
6102 stim fdem, basis, --rounds, --out-dir, --out-dem, --out-stim, --p-noise,
6103 --force-noise, --model-lb, --out-model
6104 matrices, matrix finH, finG, finL, fin, Hx, Lx, classical
6105 codewords --cws, outC, finC, maxC, dW, expand
6106 threading threads, nothrottle, chunk_size
6107 cache cache, --no-cache, --trust-start
6108 expert start, --trust-start, noscan
6109 experimental ksub, refresh
6110
6111Help options:
6112 -h, --help [TOPIC] Display summary help message (fits 80 rows); with TOPIC, the same as
6113 --morehelp TOPIC (also --help=TOPIC).
6114 --morehelp [TOPIC] Display this full help message with all parameters, or only the entries of
6115 TOPIC, e.g., --morehelp maxC (also --morehelp=TOPIC; several topics separated
6116 by commas, e.g., maxC,dW; the names are case-insensitive, without '-', '_', or
6117 '=VALUE', and include aliases such as dest or batch; an unknown name gives the
6118 closest names on stderr, and the exit code 1). A group name (see Option
6119 groups, also as singular or plural, e.g., window) gives all entries of the
6120 group, and a parameter of a group also the other entries of its group (see
6121 also).
6122 --version Display the versions of dist_m4ri.py and of the dist_m4ri binary.
6123"""
6124
6125
6126def _help_entries(text: str) -> List[Tuple[str, List[str], Dict[str, str]]]:
6127 """
6128 The entries of a help text (see _cli_morehelp_text()): (section header, the lines of the entry, its names). An
6129 entry starts with a line indented by 2 spaces (the names, then the description), and continues with the lines
6130 indented by more; a section header is a line without indentation ending with ':'. The names (a dict: normalized
6131 name -> name as written) are those in the first column (e.g., 'Hx=FILE, Hz=FILE' -> Hx, Hz; '--no-cache /
6132 nocache'), without the values (FILE, [N], ...; but all words of a note such as '(DEM codewords)'), and the aliases
6133 in the description ('alias: dest', 'Alias: win=N', 'also --no-throttle', 'also rounds=N'); normalized: lowercase,
6134 without '-' and '_'.
6135 """
6136 import re
6137 entries: List[Tuple[str, List[str], Dict[str, str]]] = []
6138 section = ""
6139 for line in text.splitlines():
6140 if line and not line[0].isspace() and line.rstrip().endswith(":"):
6141 section = line.rstrip()
6142 continue
6143 m = re.match(r"^ (\S.*?)(?:\s{2,}|$)", line)
6144 if m: # a new entry
6145 names: Dict[str, str] = {}
6146 for tok in re.split(r"[,/\s]+", m.group(1)):
6147 tok = tok.strip("()[]").split("=", 1)[0]
6148 # (not a value, e.g., FILE or N; all words of a note, e.g., '(DEM codewords)')
6149 if tok.strip("-") and (m.group(1).startswith("(") or not tok.isupper()):
6150 names.setdefault(_help_name_key(tok), tok)
6151 entries.append((section, [line], names))
6152 elif line.startswith(" ") and entries:
6153 entries[-1][1].append(line)
6154 for _, lines, names in entries:
6155 desc = " ".join(s.strip() for s in lines)
6156 for a in re.findall(r"(?i)\balias(?:es)?:\s*(-{0,2}[\w-]+)", desc) + re.findall(r"\balso (--?[\w-]+)", desc) + \
6157 re.findall(r"\balso ([\w-]+)=", desc):
6158 names.setdefault(_help_name_key(a), a)
6159 return entries
6160
6161
6162def _help_name_key(name: str) -> str:
6163 """A name of a help entry normalized for matching (see _help_entries()): lowercase, without '-' and '_'."""
6164 return name.lower().replace("-", "").replace("_", "")
6165
6166
6167def _help_group_members(entry: Tuple[str, List[str], Dict[str, str]]) -> Optional[Set[str]]:
6168 """
6169 The normalized names of the members of a group (an entry of the section 'Option groups' of the full help: the
6170 names listed after its first column), or None for another entry.
6171 """
6172 import re
6173 section, lines, _ = entry
6174 if not section.startswith("Option groups"):
6175 return None
6176 m = re.match(r"^ \S.*?(?:\s{2,}|$)", lines[0])
6177 text = " ".join([lines[0][m.end():] if m else ""] + [s.strip() for s in lines[1:]])
6178 return {_help_name_key(t) for t in re.split(r"[,\s]+", text) if t.strip("-")}
6179
6180
6181def _help_group_key_match(gkey: str, key: str) -> bool:
6182 """Whether the topic key matches the name gkey of a group, also as singular or plural (e.g., window, windows)."""
6183 return key in (gkey, gkey + "s") or (gkey.endswith("s") and key == gkey[:-1])
6184
6185
6186def print_cli_morehelp(file: Optional[Any] = None, topic: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
6187 """
6188 Prints the full help of the CLI (--morehelp), or with `topic` (one or more names separated by commas, see
6189 _help_entries()) only the entries of these parameters, in the order of the full help under their section headers.
6190 A topic may also be a group of the section 'Option groups' (also as singular or plural, e.g., window): then all
6191 its members are printed; and an entry of a group also gives the other members of its groups and these groups
6192 (one level: 'see also'). Returns 0, or 1 if some topic has no entry (then the closest names are suggested on
6193 stderr).
6194 """
6195 import difflib
6196 text = _cli_morehelp_text()
6197 keys = [(t, _help_name_key(t.split("=", 1)[0])) for t in (s.strip() for s in (topic or "").split(","))]
6198 keys = [(t, k) for t, k in keys if k]
6199 if not keys:
6200 print(text, file=file)
6201 return 0
6202 entries = _help_entries(text)
6203 members = [_help_group_members(e) for e in entries]
6204 status = 0
6205 asked: Set[int] = set()
6206 for t, key in keys:
6207 found = [i for i, e in enumerate(entries)
6208 if (key in e[2] if members[i] is None else any(_help_group_key_match(g, key) for g in e[2]))]
6209 if not found:
6210 names = {k: v for e in entries for k, v in e[2].items()}
6211 close = [names[k] for k in difflib.get_close_matches(key, list(names), n=5, cutoff=0.6)]
6212 hint = f"; did you mean {', '.join(close)}?" if close else ""
6213 sys.stderr.write(f"dist_m4ri.py: no help entry for '{t}'{hint} (--morehelp lists all parameters)\n")
6214 status = 1
6215 asked.update(found)
6216 chosen: Set[int] = set(asked)
6217 for g, mem in enumerate(members): # the groups asked for or with a member asked for: the group and its members
6218 if mem is None:
6219 continue
6220 in_group = [i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if members[i] is None and mem & set(e[2])]
6221 if g in asked or asked & set(in_group):
6222 chosen.add(g)
6223 chosen.update(in_group)
6224 out: List[str] = []
6225 section = None
6226 for i in sorted(chosen): # in the order of the full help, under their section headers
6227 sec, lines, _ = entries[i]
6228 if sec != section:
6229 if out:
6230 out.append("")
6231 out.append(sec)
6232 section = sec
6233 out.extend(lines)
6234 if out:
6235 print("\n".join(out), file=file)
6236 return status
6237
6238
6239def _warn_cli_conflicts(args: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
6240 """
6241 Writes warnings to stderr for the CLI inputs which are ignored. The input is selected in the order fdem (a DEM or
6242 a Stim circuit), Hx / Hz (a CSS code), and finH / finG / finL / fin (one sector of a quantum code, or a classical
6243 code); fin=PREFIX supplies only the missing finH (PREFIX + 'X.mtx') and finG (PREFIX + 'Z.mtx', unless finL). The
6244 disabled options --simple and --full always give a warning (see _warn_disabled_simple_full()).
6245 """
6246 def given(*keys: str) -> List[str]:
6247 return [k for k in keys if args.get(k) is not None]
6248
6249 _warn_disabled_simple_full(args.get("simple"), args.get("full"), cli=True) # (not passed on)
6250 stim_opts = [opt for opt, on in (("basis=", args.get("basis") is not None),
6251 ("--out-stim", args.get("out_stim") is not None),
6252 ("--p-noise", args.get("p_noise") is not None),
6253 ("--force-noise", bool(args.get("force_noise")))) if on]
6254 warns = []
6255 if args.get("fdem"):
6256 ign = given("finH", "finG", "finL", "fin", "Hx", "Hz", "Lx", "Lz")
6257 if ign:
6258 warns.append(f"fdem={args['fdem']} given: ignoring {', '.join(k + '=' for k in ign)}")
6259 if stim_opts and not str(args["fdem"]).endswith(".stim"):
6260 warns.append(f"{', '.join(stim_opts)}: only used for a Stim circuit (.stim); ignored")
6261 elif (args.get("basis") is not None and str(args.get("drop")).lower() != "css"
6262 and not args.get("verbose")): # (with --verbose, the basis of the classification is reported)
6263 warns.append("basis=: only used with drop=css (the minority-basis detectors of a CSS circuit); ignored")
6264 if args.get("expand") and not (args.get("outC") or args.get("do_cws")):
6265 warns.append("expand=: only used with outC= or --cws; ignored")
6266 else:
6267 dem_opts = stim_opts + [opt for opt, on in (("--out-dir", args.get("out_dir") is not None),
6268 ("--out-dem", args.get("out_dem") is not None)) if on]
6269 if (args.get("pmin") or 0.0) > 0.0:
6270 dem_opts.append("pmin=")
6271 if args.get("merge") is not None:
6272 dem_opts.append("merge=")
6273 if args.get("expand") is not None:
6274 dem_opts.append("expand=")
6275 if args.get("drop") is not None:
6276 dem_opts.append("drop=")
6277 if args.get("outD") is not None:
6278 dem_opts.append("outD=")
6279 if args.get("out_reduced") is not None:
6280 dem_opts.append("--out-reduced")
6281 if dem_opts:

6311 ("solver=", args.get("solver") not in (None, "dist_m4ri"))) if on]
